The security deposit may not exceed three months' rent. The sum must be placed in a blocked account in the tenant's name. For anyone signing or renewing a lease, the check is straightforward: compare the amount requested with the limit and check that the account is in the name of the person renting the accommodation. The rule is not cantonal: it belongs to the federal framework and applies in the same way throughout the country.
The second step concerns the landlord's termination notice. The notice is valid only if made on an official cantonal form. In the canton of Vaud, therefore, the form's format must be checked as a local element, without confusing it with the federal rule governing tenancy. The distinction is useful for those moving between cantons: the basic law remains the same, while the form is specified at cantonal level.
If the tenant wants to challenge the termination notice, they must contact the conciliation authority within 30 days. The deadline is defined by the source and must be treated as a procedural deadline: the challenge should not be left to an informal check of the form. For a reader in Vaud, the operational point is therefore to note the 30-day deadline and the competent authority immediately.
The national comparison of the 2026 real estate market thus starts from four verifiable elements: deposit, blocked account, official form and challenge deadline. To assess the impact of a rent on the budget, the contract amount should be considered alongside the cost of living in Switzerland. The source mentions items that belong to different levels: taxation, health insurance and social contributions. Separating them helps avoid attributing to one body a responsibility that belongs to another.

Swiss taxation has three levels: direct federal tax, cantonal tax and municipal tax. Each canton has its own law and multiplier; municipalities apply a multiplier to cantonal tax. Therefore, when comparing budgets, there is no single local rule that applies everywhere.

### The day of the grounding On October 2, 2001, after 4:00 p.m., the Swissair grounding turned a working day into a rupture for the entire staff. Sandrine Nikolic-Fuss, today president of the Kapers cabin crew union and a former company employee, was not on duty: she was six months pregnant and followed the event from the ground.
Before the grounding, warning signs had emerged, but when everything came to a standstill, reality seemed completely unreal to her. The aircraft remained on the ground, passengers were stranded somewhere in the world, and the crews did not know how they would continue working.
For Nikolic-Fuss, the collapse affected more than just one company. With Swissair, a national symbol in which Switzerland had long recognized itself sank. The employees lost what she calls their professional home, a loss that could not simply be digested. Even years later, the trade unionist could not shake the feeling that Switzerland had left her alone. Those who had lived through that day had seen how quickly something considered unshakable could be destroyed.
At the decisive moment, neither personal commitment nor years of loyalty managed to protect the employees. For Nikolic-Fuss, it was a watershed that shaped her work as a trade unionist. Integration into the Lufthansa Group may have saved Swiss aviation economically, but it did not erase the lesson of the grounding: economic success and the strength of a brand are not enough on their own to guarantee secure jobs and reliable conditions.
Since 2001, she adds, the industry has changed profoundly. External crises, strong cost pressure, competition, working conditions and contracts have entered a phase of increasing pressure. The trade unionist does not claim that everything was better back then; she does, however, recall a stronger awareness of the value of trained and experienced staff. At Swissair, people did not simply feel employed, but part of a company, a history and a special professional culture. ## The work the brand does not tell
### From the uniform to the responsibilities The most concrete part of the testimony concerns what happens inside the cabin. From the outside, the work of flight attendants is often reduced to onboard service. Nikolic-Fuss instead highlights evacuations, firefighting, first aid and critical decisions. This distinction changes how a job is viewed: the company’s image does not encompass the responsibility entrusted to the staff.

The third dimension is the team. In confined spaces, one must remain calm, be flexible and rely on one another. From this emerge a particular solidarity and a strong team spirit: elements that do not erase fatigue or uncertainty, but explain why the profession left such a profound mark on the unionist’s life.
The comparison between then and now should not, however, be reduced to nostalgia for Swissair. Nikolic-Fuss admits that not everything was better back then. The point is another: at the company, the staff felt part of a company, a history and a special professional culture; today, before choosing, the same person would reflect longer on hours, health, family, salary and contract. Noting these elements before choosing helps compare enthusiasm for flying with the reality of the job.
### 3. Assess training and the team The source highlights the value of trained and experienced staff and the qualities needed on board: calm, flexibility and mutual trust in confined spaces. For this reason, the choice concerns more than just the brand. One must ask whether one’s way of working is compatible with critical responsibilities, international teams and solidarity built during service.
### 4. Balance motivation and prudence Nikolic-Fuss’s experience shows that the profession can broaden horizons through encounters with people from different cultures, work in international groups and direct experience of the world. The final criterion can be put this way: the desire to fly must hold up even after considering health, family, salary and contract. The jump came as energy prices accelerated. According to Eurostat, the increase in energy prices reached 18,8% in September, compared with 14,3% in the previous month. The source links the surge in energy prices to the conflict in the Middle East.
### Energy and the ECB's response
The overall figure thus rose to almost twice the 2% target set by the ECB. The acceleration weighs on European households and businesses, according to the description provided along with the first estimate.
In recent months, price pressures have pushed the ECB to tighten monetary policy. The institution has already raised its key interest rates twice during the year, bringing the main rate to 2,5%.
The central bank has not formally ruled out further monetary tightening in the coming months. The stated reason is price pressures, while the report attributes September's acceleration to the surge in the energy component.

item.title: Average salary professions Switzerland 2026: canton Aargau
item.description: Comparison 2026 between professions, sectors and cantons: the focus on Aargau starts with taxes, AVS/AI/IPG contributions, LPP and LAMal.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - The 2026 comparison distinguishes cantons, sectors, and the canton of Aargau - The Swiss tax system operates on three levels - AHV/IV/EO: 5.3% borne by the employee - The KVG/LAMal is not a salary deduction
## Key facts - Comparison → cantons, sectors, and canton of Aargau - Tax → Federal direct tax (IFD), cantonal and municipal taxes - AHV/IV/EO → 5.3% employee; 10.6% total - ALV/AC → 1.1% up to the annual ceiling - UVG/LAA → 0.7–1.5% depending on the sector - BVG/LPP → 7%, 10%, 15%, 18% depending on age - KVG/LAMal → mandatory for residents - Maximum working hours → 45 or 50 hours per week
Three tax levels act as the first filter for reading the average salary by profession in Switzerland. The federal direct tax is complemented by cantonal and municipal taxes. Each canton has its own law and multiplier; municipalities apply a multiplier to the cantonal tax. For the canton of Aargau, a national comparison must therefore also indicate the territorial level to which it refers.
### Competencies not to be confused Institutional competencies are not interchangeable. The FTA/ESTV manages the federal direct tax and VAT; cantonal administrations handle the cantonal and municipal components. The FSIO/BSV concerns social security, including AHV/IV/BVG, but does not set taxes. The FSO/BFS produces statistics and does not establish rates.
On the salary, AHV/IV/EO are at 5.3% for the employee and 10.6% in total with the employer. ALV/AC is at 1.1% up to the annual ceiling. UVG/LAA varies between 0.7% and 1.5% depending on the sector. For BVG/LPP, on the coordinated salary, the rates are 7% between 25 and 34 years old, 10% between 35 and 44, 15% between 45 and 54, and 18% from 55 years old until the reference age.
The labor framework completes the data: there is no federal minimum wage, although some cantons have their own. The maximum working time is 45 hours per week in industry, offices, and retail, or 50 hours in other sectors. Minimum vacation is four weeks, five for those under 20 years old. Maternity leave lasts 14 weeks at 80% through EO, and paternity leave lasts two weeks. Notice periods are one, two, or three months depending on seniority. The median salary falls within the figures indexed each year: for 2026, the value used as a reference must therefore be checked in the official source. ## From salary to budget
### Four items to separate A salary figure should not be read as an isolated amount. To compare the canton of Aargau with the national picture, it is useful to separate the items related to salary from the costs that remain distinct. The following grid brings together the percentages and rules to keep alongside the professional figure:
| Item | Rule | How to use it | |---|---|---| | AVS/AI/IPG | 5,3% employee; 10,6% total with the employer | Separate the individual and total shares | | AD/AC | 1,1% up to the annual maximum | Consider the limit without inventing an amount | | LAINF/LAA | 0,7–1,5% depending on the sector | Link the item to the sector | | LPP/BVG | 7%, 10%, 15% and 18% of the coordinated salary, depending on age | Use the correct bracket |
The percentages show why profession, sector and age are not interchangeable variables. The LAINF/LAA rate is linked to the sector, LPP changes bracket with age and AD/AC provides for an annual maximum. A comparison between offers must report these three elements alongside the salary figure, instead of summarizing them in a single result.
### LAMal remains separate LAMal/KVG is mandatory for anyone residing in Switzerland and must be taken out within three months of arrival. It is private insurance with per-capita premiums: it is not a tax and is not a salary contribution. For adults, the deductibles are CHF 300, 500, 1000, 1500, 2000 or 2500. Premiums depend on the canton and region, while premium reductions are cantonal. To measure purchasing power, therefore place the salary alongside costo della vita in Svizzera, without including the LAMal premium among salary deductions.
### Taxes and local rules The tax component follows three levels: federal IFD, cantonal and municipal taxes. Since each canton has its own law and multiplier and the municipality applies a multiplier to the cantonal tax, the Aargau-Switzerland comparison must always indicate the territorial scope. Employment conditions also affect how the offer is assessed: maximum working hours, holidays, maternity, paternity and termination belong to the same practical assessment, even though they are not salary amounts.
## Useful planning tools To estimate your pension strategy, use the pension planner and the pillar 3 simulator. ## Operational Procedure
### Five checks before the comparison
1. Territorial scope. Specify profession, sector, canton, and municipality. If the reference is the canton of Aargau, do not mix the cantonal level with the municipal one: the tax system provides for both, and the municipality applies a multiplier on the cantonal tax.
2. Salary items. Use a Swiss payslip as a reading grid and separate AHV/IV/EO, ALV/AC, UVG/LAA, and BVG/LPP. Report 5.3% for the employee share of AHV/IV/EO, 1.1% for ALV/AC up to the annual ceiling, and the UVG/LAA rate between 0.7% and 1.5% depending on the sector.
3. Social security. For BVG/LPP, place the employee in the correct coordinated salary bracket: 7% between 25 and 34 years old, 10% between 35 and 44, 15% between 45 and 54, and 18% from 55 years old until the reference age. Do not use a single rate for all ages.
4. Healthcare and taxes. If the person resides in Switzerland, verify the LAMal/KVG insurance within three months of arrival and consider an adult deductible between CHF 300 and 2500 according to the indicated options. Premiums depend on the canton and region, and premium reduction is cantonal. For the tax part, refer to the tax return: Direct Federal Tax (IFD/DFD) and VAT fall under the Federal Tax Administration (AFC/ESTV), while the cantonal and municipal levels are managed by cantonal administrations.
5. Contract and status. Check for the absence of a federal minimum wage and verify if the canton applies its own. Also, compare the 45 or 50-hour limit, minimum vacation days, leave, and notice periods. For foreign workers, the SEM distinguishes between the short-term L permit (up to one year), the renewable B permit, the C settlement permit (usually after 10 years of residence or 5 years for EU/EFTA citizens), and the G permit for cross-border commuters.
For statistics, the FSO/BFS is the reference body but does not set tax rates. The FSIO/BSV deals with social security and not taxes. This separation avoids using salary statistics for tax calculations or a LAMal/KVG premium as a salary contribution.
To transform the comparison into a readable figure, use the salary calculator.

item.title: Gotthard: data analysis to avoid queues
item.description: Fabrizio Bacchini created the Gottardo Live app by analyzing 19 thousand FEDRO reports. Find out how to monitor traffic and better plan your trip.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - Bacchini analyzes the traffic of the Gotthard every day. - From 11 July, traffic jams on 82 out of 83 days. - On July 18, the queue reached 20 kilometers. - The Gottardo Live app uses official data.
## Key Facts - Who is frequency → Fabrizio Bacchini, a 57-year-old manager from Zug; four-five monthly crossings - Data analyzed → about 19 thousand reports since the beginning of July - Peak → 20 kilometers of queue and 200 minutes of waiting on July 18 - Critical → from 11 am to 6 pm - App and threshold → Gotthard Live, free of charge; 10-20 minutes of traffic jam acceptable
### Monitoring built on data
In the text of 2 October 2026, Fabrizio Bacchini's story tells how an everyday mobility problem became a digital project. The 57-year-old manager from Zug crosses the Gotthard tunnel four to five times a month for work. To decide when to leave, he checks traffic data every day and looks for the moment when the queue starts to shrink.
Since the beginning of July, it has sifted through about 19 thousand official reports. Its system records waiting times, expressed in minutes, and the length of queues, indicated in kilometers, for both directions of travel every five minutes. The basis is the communications of the Federal Roads Office, FEDRO. Official warnings on accidents, road closures and traffic flow regulations are also included in the monitoring.
The result returns the frequency of the problem. Since 11 July, traffic jams have been recorded in front of the tunnel on 82 out of 83 days. The peak came on Saturday 18 July, with 20 kilometres of queues southbound and waiting times of up to 200 minutes. In September, outside of holiday periods, traffic jams formed every weekday.
The slot between 11 and 18 is practically always congested. Bacchini, on the other hand, indicates early morning and late afternoon as the times that usually offer the best conditions. However, the choice also depends on the day of the week: looking at the map, it follows the moment when the queue begins to shorten.
Passion led to the birth of Gottardo Live, a free app that uses official data and signals when the traffic jam forms, lengthens or begins to dissolve. Bacchini says he programmed it to retrieve information every five minutes, then checking it with webcams and the real situation. At the beginning, he dedicated up to five hours a day to the project. Today the system is more stable, but continues to check the data daily. ## What changes for those who have to go through the tunnel
For those who live or work in Switzerland and have to travel the southern axis, the material collected by Bacchini offers a practical reading: traffic should not be considered only as an event related to holidays. The observed series, on the other hand, shows a recurring presence, with a central band of the day almost always difficult and with differences related to the weekly calendar.
### From photography to decision
The useful distinction is between the historical data and the real-time situation. Comparisons between individual days serve to recognize patterns: when the traffic jam tends to form, when it reaches its longest phase and when it begins to dissolve. The app notification follows precisely these phases. For those who have to organize a crossing, the most informative moment is not necessarily the one when the queue is already at its maximum, but the one when the map shows a change. This is the logic that Bacchini applies when he observes the beginning of the reduction of the column.
The time slot indicated by his analysis can be read as a grid, not as a promise. Between 11 and 18 congestion is described as practically constant; early morning and late afternoon are the windows that are usually better. The day of the week remains an autonomous variable. The fact that in September traffic jams occurred every weekday prevents the problem from being reduced to only large exoduses.
The comparison with the previous situation is also concrete. Bacchini explains that an app already existed, but it was full of advertising and forced people to search within it for traffic information. Gottardo Live was created to directly use official data and report the evolution of the queue. This makes the reading described in the story more immediate, without turning the app into a rule that is the same for every motorist.
The limit of ten or twenty minutes is Bacchini's personal one: beyond that threshold, he prefers to take the pace. It is not a threshold attributed to the road network nor a general recommendation. It is an example of how a measured figure can become an individual choice.
For those who want to combine the reading of traffic with a comparison with mezzi pubblici, however, this is another evaluation plan. The same goes for the costo della vita in Svizzera: history does not offer figures on this aspect, so it is not possible to derive an economic cost from the kilometers of queue.
## Recommended tools For an updated estimate, use the net salary calculator and the CHF-EUR exchange comparator. ## How to use analytics before you go
The story allows you to derive an operational sequence based only on the available information. There is no need to transform the app into a fixed calendar: the method consists of verifying the update, reading the queue phase and comparing the data with the observed patterns.
### Four essential steps
1. Open Gotthard Live and start with the official data. The app is free of charge and uses FEDRO reports. The reference must be the current situation, because the system collects data every five minutes.
2. Check both directions of travel. The information considered by Bacchini includes waiting times in minutes and queue length in kilometers. Before deciding, it is therefore necessary to distinguish the south direction from the opposite one, without automatically transferring data to the other direction.
3. Read the movement of the queue. The signal does not only concern the presence of the traffic jam: it indicates whether it is forming, if it is lengthening or if it is beginning to dissolve. Push notifications must be interpreted with the same care with which Bacchini has adjusted their frequency, avoiding an arrival too early or too close.
4. Compare the update with the day and time. His analysis identifies recurrences, but leaves room for checking the moment. Early morning and late afternoon are the references indicated as generally best; the time slot between 11 and 18 is the one described as congested. If the wait exceeds the personal threshold, Bacchini's criterion is to take the pace.
This procedure serves to distinguish official data, their evolution and individual decision. For those who cross the tunnel for work, it concerns first of all the time of the journey; the other economic aspects remain separate from the traffic analysis.
The project shows how much work there is behind a seemingly simple notice: scheduling data recovery, comparing it with webcams, checking the real situation and adjusting notifications. Those who use the app can limit themselves to the final result, while the daily check remains the step that makes the update readable. item.description: Novartis obtains the worldwide license on ABO2203 from Abogen: 575 million initial dollars and potential payments up to about 7.2 billion.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - Novartis obtains worldwide license on ABO2203. - Abogen receives an initial $575 million. - The agreement can reach about 7.2 billion. - ABO2203 mRNA is used against B lymphocytes.
## Key Facts - Active ingredient: ABO2203 - License: Worldwide Exclusive - Initial payment: $575 million - Value: CHF 480 million - Potential: up to approximately $7.2 billion - Technology: mRNA - Development: clinical phase
### The structure of the agreement Novartis expands its portfolio of RNA-based therapeutics thanks to a license agreement with Abogen Biosciences, a Chinese biotech company. The agreement was communicated by Abogen itself in a note.
At the heart is ABO2203, a new active ingredient for the treatment of autoimmune diseases. The agreement gives Novartis an exclusive worldwide license on the active ingredient and provides options on additional drug programs based on Abogen's RNA platform.
The expected initial payment for Abogen is $575 million, or CHF 480 million. The potential portion of the transaction can be as high as $7.2 billion if all options on the other programs are exercised and the respective development, approval and commercialization milestones are met.
Abogen will also be entitled to possible licensing revenue on future sales of the products. The structure therefore combines an initial component, a part related to milestones and a possible return on sales.
### How does ABO2203 ABO2203 uses mRNA, the messenger ribonucleic acid, to induce the body to produce a molecule on its own that attacks and eliminates B lymphocytes in a targeted manner. These cells play an important role in many autoimmune diseases. According to Abogen, the drug is already in clinical development.
RNA technology had made a lot of headlines especially thanks to the Covid vaccines from Moderna and Biontech. However, it has existed for several decades and had previously been tested mainly in cancer research. The press release thus puts in the same agreement an active ingredient already in clinical development and a platform from which other programs can derive. ## What does potential value mean
To read the agreement from an economic point of view, it is necessary to keep separate the initial payment, the conditions for subsequent payments and the possible revenues related to sales. The figure of about 7.2 billion is not presented as an initial outlay: the source links it to the exercise of all options and the achievement of the expected goals.
### The components of the agreement
| Voice | Practical reading | |---|---| | Initial payment | USD 575 million, with an indicated value of CHF 480 million. | | Options | Additional programs based on Abogen's RNA platform. | | Milestones | Development, approval and commercialisation of the programmes concerned. | | Future Sales | Possible licensing revenue for Abogen. |
The correct comparison is therefore not between two sums available at the same time. The $575 million is reported as the initial payment; instead, the maximum value depends on a sequence of conditions. All options for the other programs must be exercised first, then the respective development, approval, and commercialization milestones must be met.
For a reader in Switzerland, the reference to 480 million francs makes the scale of the initial component immediate, while the total potential remains expressed in dollars. The currency, however, does not change the structure of the agreement: the first amount and the maximum potential belong to different times and conditions.
The scientific profile must also be read separately from the commercial one. ABO2203 is described as already in clinical development, but the agreement also links additional payments to approval and marketing. The text therefore distinguishes the development of the drug from the steps necessary to get to sales.
For the daily life of residents, the concrete connection remains informative: the source describes a transaction between companies, not a payment intended for families. To distinguish the company figure from one's income, you can use the calcolatore stipendio; those who want to follow the labor market can consult the aziende che assumono.
## Useful tools to protect your net income To reduce FX leakage, compare CHF-EUR exchange options and banks for cross-border workers. ## A control board for the reader
### Five operational steps
1. **Identify the object.** The first reference is ABO2203, an active ingredient intended for the treatment of autoimmune diseases. This avoids confusing it with the broader RNA-based platform.
2. Separate license and options. The license granted to Novartis is exclusive and worldwide for ABO2203. The options instead cover additional drug programs based on Abogen's RNA platform.
3. Record the amount and currency. The initial payment should be recorded as 575 million dollars, with the indicated equivalent of 480 million francs. The two figures describe the same initial payment, not two separate payments.
4. Rebuild the condition for the maximum. The value of up to about $7.2 billion requires the exercise of all options and the achievement of development, approval and commercialization goals. The figure should therefore be read as a scenario subject to these steps.
5. Keep future sales separate. Abogen may have possible license revenue on future product sales. This item should not be confused with either the initial payment or the milestones listed above.
The reading procedure allows you to update the news without adding external estimates. Each new element should be traced back to one of five steps: the active ingredient, options, initial amount, milestones or future sales.
On a scientific level, two pieces of information from the source remain central: ABO2203 mRNA is used to target B lymphocytes and the drug is already in clinical development. On the economic level, however, the decisive fact is the distinction between the initial payment and payments subject to subsequent phases.
To keep the agreement data separate from your income, use the calcolatore stipendio.

item.description: 2026 comparison between professions, cantons and sectors: AHV contributions, BVG, taxes on three levels and KVG to read the canton of St. Gallen.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - No federal minimum wage; some cantons have one - AHV/IV/EO: 5.3% to be paid by the employee - KVG mandatory for residents within 3 months of arrival - Taxation is federal, cantonal and municipal
## Key Facts - Focus → canton of St. Gallen and national comparison - FSO/BFS → statistics - AHV/IV/EO → 5.3% employee, 10.6% total with employer - AD/AC → 1.1% up to the annual ceiling - UVG/LAA → 0.7–1.5% depending on the sector - Maximum hours → 45 or 50 hours per week - Minimum holidays → 4 weeks, 5 under 20 years old - Maternity → 14 weeks at 80% through EO
5.3% of AHV/IV/EO contributions are paid by the employee, while the total with the employer reaches 10.6%. It is the first step to read the average salary by profession in Switzerland in 2026 without confusing the gross with what remains in the paycheck in the canton of St. Gallen.
For statistics, the reference is FSO/BFS. The median salary is one of the figures indexed each year: the precise amounts must be checked against the correct year and the official source. An unverified value cannot become a 2026 figure attributed to a profession or the canton of St. Gallen.
### The tax perimeter The tax framework follows a separate logic. In Switzerland, there are three levels: direct federal tax, cantonal tax and municipal tax. Each canton has its own law and multiplier; the municipality applies a multiplier on the cantonal tax. FTA/ESTV manages IFD and VAT, cantonal administrations cantonal and municipal taxation. FSO/BFS produces statistics, does not set rates; FSIO/BSV concerns social security and does not set taxes.
### Payroll Entries The transition from gross to net requires isolating contributions. AHV/IV/EO is 5.3% for the employee and 10.6% overall with the employer. AD/CA is 1.1% up to the annual ceiling. UVG/LAA is indicated between 0.7% and 1.5% depending on the sector. BVG is calculated on the coordinated salary: 7% between 25 and 34 years old, 10% between 35 and 44, 15% between 45 and 54, 18% from 55 years old up to the reference age.
The minimum wage completes the reading of the labor market: there is no federal threshold, while some cantons have their own rules. Working conditions also matter: the maximum working time is 45 hours per week in industry, offices and sales, or 50 in other sectors; holidays are at least four weeks, five under the age of 20. Maternity lasts 14 weeks at 80% through EO and paternity leave two weeks.
For a first simulation of the transition from gross to net, the calcolatore stipendio can be used. ### Three accounts not to be mixed A useful comparison for the canton of St. Gallen should put three levels on the same sheet: salary data, deductions and departures that are not withheld. The median salary is among the figures indexed each year; for 2026, only the value for the correct year should be used. A salary statistic does not describe the net or the cost of living on its own.
| Voice | Practical question | |---|---| | Salary | Which profession, industry and year are compared? | | BVG | Which age group and coordinated salary apply? | | KVG | Which canton or region, deductible and premium reduction? | | Taxes | Which three levels and which municipal multiplier? | | Cost of living | Which expenses are left out of the paycheck? |
The easiest place to make mistakes is the KVG. For residents, it is mandatory and must be taken out within 3 months of arrival, but it works with per capita premiums: it is not a tax and it is not a wage contribution. The premiums depend on the canton and region, while the premium reduction is cantonal. For adults, the deductibles indicated are CHF 300, 500, 1000, 1500, 2000 and 2500.
For the same gross, the result may change if the relevant age group for the BVG, the canton or region of the KVG and the tax municipality change. In the canton of St. Gallen, the municipal multiplier must therefore be kept separate from the cantonal law: the municipality applies its own multiplier on the cantonal tax. Without an updated official rate, an invented percentage does not have to be entered. VAT also remains within the federal tax perimeter of the FTA/ESTV, not among the withholdings to be confused with AHV, ALV, UVG or BVG.
To complete the picture of expenses, place the costo della vita in Svizzera next to it and check the LAMal e cassa malati.
## Useful tools to protect your net income To reduce FX leakage, compare CHF-EUR exchange options and banks for cross-border workers. ## How to check an offer for 2026
### Five-Step Procedure 1. Define the scope. Write down the profession, industry, canton of St. Gallen and year 2026. Look up the statistical data at FSO/BFS and check that any median salary refers to the correct year. Do not replace a missing figure with an estimate.
2. Start from gross. Separate AHV/IV/EO, ALV/CA, UVG/LAA and BVG. Record 5.3% payable by the employee for AHV/IV/EO, 10.6% overall with the employer, 1.1% ALV/AC up to the annual ceiling and 0.7–1.5% UVG/LAA depending on the sector. For BVG, use the coordinated salary and the expected age group.
3. Add the KVG. If you live in Switzerland, you must take out insurance within 3 months of arrival. The premium is per capita, not a tax or a wage contribution; check canton or region, adult deductible and possible cantonal reduction. The deductibles indicated are CHF 300, 500, 1000, 1500, 2000 or 2500.
4. Reconstruct the tax system. Divide direct federal, cantonal and municipal tax. For IFD and VAT, the reference is FTA/ESTV; for cantonal and municipal taxes, the cantonal administrations. Consider the multiplier of the municipality, without assigning rates to FSO/BFS or FSIO/BSV.
5. Check the contract. Check the minimum wage: there is no federal threshold, but some cantons have their own. Then compare maximum hours, holidays, maternity, paternity and termination: 45 or 50 hours depending on the sector, at least 4 weeks of vacation, 14 weeks of maternity leave at 80%, 2 weeks of paternity leave; the termination is 1 month in the first year, 2 from the second to the ninth and 3 from the tenth.
To sort the busta paga svizzera entries and link them to the cost of living, use a simulation consistent with the year and canton. For the final net calculation, open the calcolatore stipendio.

### The perimeter of the start Opening a business in the canton of Graubünden requires keeping the corporate project and the cost of management separate. The choice of legal form, registration in the commercial register, minimum capital, registration fees and insurance obligations belong to the same path, but they are not the same item. An orderly estimate must therefore distinguish what is needed to start the business from what is used with taxation and wages.
The first reference is the tax system. In Switzerland, the levy has three levels: direct federal tax, cantonal tax and municipal tax. Each canton has its own law and multiplier; the municipality applies a multiplier on the cantonal tax. Administrative responsibilities must also be divided. The FTA/ESTV deals with direct federal tax and VAT. The cantonal administrations manage the cantonal and municipal components. The FSIO/BSV covers social security, including AHV/IV and BVG, but does not set taxes. The FSO/BFS produces statistics and does not set rates. For a new job, confusing these roles can lead to putting the correct entry in front of the wrong office.
The practical point is to separate the opening cost from the operating cost. The registration fees belong to the start-up; taxation, on the other hand, follows the three levels provided, while insurance obligations can be linked to salaries or, for the KVG, to residence. To prepare the dichiarazione delle imposte, it is advisable to keep the entries in the register, tax and insurance separate from the start. ## From the register to recurring costs

Record commercial register fees as a separate entry and do not merge them with future taxes or payroll contributions. The distinction makes it possible to understand which disbursements belong to the opening and which to the management. 3. Separate tax competences. For direct federal tax and VAT, the reference is the FTA/ESTV; for the cantonal and municipal part, the cantonal administrations are responsible. The municipal multiplier should be read as applied to the cantonal tax, within a three-tier system. 4. Prepare the work block. If there are salaries, set up the calculation with AHV/IV/EO, ALV/CA, UVG/LAA and BVP/BVG. Use the annual ceiling of the ALV/HC, the sector for the UVG/LAA and the salary coordinated with the age group for the BVG, without replacing these parameters with outdated amounts. 5. Check residence and staff rules. For residents, the KVG must be concluded within three months of arrival; premiums and reductions depend on the canton and region. If you are hiring, plan schedules, holidays, maternity, paternity and notice periods according to the indicated limits.
The check does not end with registration. For this reason, a quote built with a fixed figure risks quickly becoming outdated: the parameters must be updated on the official source before using them.

item.title: Guy Parmelin announces his resignation from the Federal Council
item.description: The head of the Federal Department of Economic Affairs will leave office on 31 December 2026. Excluding health reasons: 'I feel a certain tiredness'.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - Parmelin to leave the Federal Council on 31 December - Health is not the reason for resignation - The Jans hypothesis opens up on the EAER - Duties, agriculture and housing await the successor
## Key Facts - Decision → resignation from the Federal Council - Deadline → 31 December - Place of announcement → Bern - Current position → Head of the Federal Department of Economic Affairs - Stated reason → a certain tiredness - Hypothesis for EAER → Jans - Themes for the successor → US tariffs, agriculture and housing
### The conference in Bern On 2 October 2026, at 11 a.m., Guy Parmelin convened a press conference in Bern at short notice. The Federal Councillor, currently head of the Federal Department of Economic Affairs, announced his decision to resign from the Federal Council at the end of the year. He will cease his duties on 31 December.
The first clarification concerned health. In front of the media, Parmelin said that his condition had nothing to do with the choice. Back pain had repeatedly fueled speculation in the media about a possible resignation, but the president of the Confederation separated that issue from the political decision.
> "I feel a certain tiredness: the sacred fire is no longer as sacred as it was at the beginning."
Parmelin explained that he had thought long and hard during the summer break about what was best for the country. Progressively, he added, retiring at the end of the year seemed to him to be the most appropriate decision. He also said that he had taken enormous pleasure in leading the department and wanted to make room for new forces in times of great uncertainty.
The President of the Confederation reported that he had informed his colleagues that morning, during the weekly meeting of the executive. However, he did not consider his work finished: he said that he was still motivated, that he wanted to face the remaining challenges and that he would work until 31 December at 23:59. He also recalled that there will be a popular vote and that he intends to work to ensure that the voice of the Federal Council is heard by the population.
For the succession, the Jans hypothesis is open. The text indicates, among the challenges of the future responsible, US tariffs, agriculture and housing. A final decision on the name of the successor is not indicated. ## The significance of the passage for Switzerland
The news opens a passage at the top of Swiss economic policy, but does not yet describe a concrete change for those who live or work in the country. The source communicates the exit of Guy Parmelin, the end of his mandate and the existence of a hypothesis for succession. However, he does not indicate a new measure, a figure or a personal procedure related to the resignation.
The possible change at the helm of the DFE, indicated as EAER in the titles, must therefore be read through the three dossiers mentioned for the successor: US tariffs, agriculture and housing. These are issues explicitly associated with the phase that is opening, not decisions already taken. The source does not provide amounts, a timetable for measures or indications on the line that Jans would follow. Transforming the hypothesis into an announcement of concrete change would therefore anticipate the available information.
| Theme | Status in Source | Operational Reading | |---|---|---| | Succession | Parmelin leaves on December 31 | Jans' name is still presented as a hypothesis | | Agenda | U.S. Tariffs, Agriculture & Homes | No Measurements or Figures Are Stated | | Continuity | Parmelin says he will work until 23:59 | The text does not describe the handover | | Early 2027 | Parmelin and Helene Budliger Artieda to leave their positions | Parmelin recalls the existence of replacements |
### The double passage of 2027 For the reader, the most delicate point is to distinguish the calendar from the political forecast. At the beginning of 2027, according to the source, Parmelin and State Secretary Helene Budliger Artieda will no longer hold their posts. Parmelin does not see a problem with the departure of two key figures in Swiss economic policy: he argues that no one is irreplaceable and that those in managerial positions have replacements.
Parties and associations are divided on the future of the Federal Council, but the text does not report the individual positions. The usable datum is therefore the existence of a confrontation, not its outcome or a precise proposal.
The dossier of the manufacturers can be followed, from the reader's point of view, together with the costo della vita in Svizzera; the source text, however, does not contain figures or forecasts on this topic. The same caution applies to the other two dossiers indicated: until the succession is defined, it is not possible to attribute to the future manager decisions that the source does not announce.
## Recommended tools For an updated estimate, use the net salary calculator and the CHF-EUR exchange comparator. ## How to follow developments without anticipating decisions
### Four useful steps First: set the certain timetable. The announcement was made on October 2, 2026 in Bern, while the exit from the Federal Council is scheduled for December 31. Parmelin said that he will continue to work until 23:59; this is the operational deadline indicated in the text.
Second: separate the decision from the hypothesis. The resignation was announced directly by Parmelin. Jans, on the other hand, appears as a possibility for the leadership of the EAER. When reading the next updates, it is advisable to keep the certain news distinct from the name still hypothesized.
Third: follow the three issues associated with the successor without turning them into measures already approved. US tariffs, agriculture and housing are presented as challenges. The source does not indicate either a measure or a figure linked to these dossiers, so any assessment must start from what will actually be announced.
Fourthly, to keep the succession separate from the popular vote mentioned by Parmelin. The Federal Councillor has said that he intends to work to ensure that the voice of the Federal Council is heard by the population, but the text does not specify the subject of the vote. It is therefore not possible to add details on its content.
The reference to the new forces concerns institutional replacement, not an announcement of hiring. Those who want to keep the two plans distinct can consult the annunci di lavoro, without presenting the Jans hypothesis as an already defined candidacy.

## In brief - The Federal Council took note of the report on 2 October 2026 - The inventory covers facilities with an initial capacity of at least 10 kW - Those active in 1914 and still existing today are included - The report complements the statistics on facilities of at least 300 kW
## Key facts - Publication → 2 October 2026 - Location → Bern - Body → Federal Council - Mandate → postulate 24.3007 of CAPTE-S - Historical criterion → initial capacity of at least 10 kilowatts - Reference year → 1914 - Complementary statistics → installed capacity of at least 300 kilowatts - Document → 1.77 MB PDF
On 2 October 2026, at its meeting in Bern, the Federal Council took note of the report in fulfilment of postulate 24.3007 of the Environment, Spatial Planning and Energy Committee of the Council of States, referred to in the communiqué by the acronym CAPTE-S. The communiqué presents the act as the taking note of the report, published as a Federal Council document.
The report has a defined scope. It provides an overview of hydroelectric facilities with an initial capacity of at least 10 kilowatts that were in operation in the reference year 1914 and still exist today. The three elements must be read together: the initial-capacity threshold, operation in the specified year and the continued existence of the facility.
### What Bern publishes
The inventory concerns historic hydroelectric facilities in Switzerland. The communiqué presents it as a complement, not a replacement, to the statistics on Switzerland's hydroelectric facilities. The latter records operating facilities with an installed capacity of at least 300 kilowatts.
The distinction is essential for reading the document correctly. The historical inventory uses the initial capacity and the threshold of 10 kilowatts; the statistics referred to use the installed capacity and the threshold of 300 kilowatts. The time criterion is also different: for the inventory, the reference to 1914 and the existence indicated by the source matter, while the description of the statistics is limited to operating facilities.
The text released on 2 October does not state the number of facilities, their locations, the capacity of each one or any subsequent interventions. These data cannot be added to the news item without consulting the report. The available reference is the PDF Inventar der historischen Wasserkraftanlagen in der Schweiz: Bericht des Bundesrates, published on 2 October 2026 and indicated as having a size of 1.77 MB.
For a separate overview of personal expenses, costo della vita in Svizzera remains a distinct tool: the communiqué does not quantify costs, tariffs or amounts for households.
For the national public, the key point is not the announcement of a new single threshold for all facilities. The source presents two complementary surveys, with different reference units. Anyone reading the inventory must therefore preserve the distinction between historical and statistical data, without turning the threshold of one survey into the threshold of the other. The difference between inventory and statistics changes the way you have to read a data sheet or a reference to a plant. It is not enough to find the word hydroelectric: you have to understand which survey you are using and what power is indicated. The press release does not offer elements to add the two sets or to treat them as if they had the same requirement.
### Two criteria, two readings
| Detection | Indicated power | Time or status criterion | | Historical inventory | at least 10 kW of initial power | in operation in 1914 and still existing | | Swiss Statistics | at least 300 kW installed capacity | system in operation |
The table shows the distinctions contained in the press release. In the first case, the combination of the three filters leads to a historical snapshot: initial power threshold, operation in the reference year 1914 and permanence of the plant. In the second case, the statistics consider the plants in operation and use the installed power as a parameter.
The source does not say that a system present in the first panel must also appear in the second. For this reason, when comparing the documents, you must first check the threshold and then the type of power. It is a simple step, but avoid reading the 10 kW as if they were 10 kW installed or the 300 kW as a criterion of the historical inventory.
The scope of the information also remains delimited. The press release does not quantify production, does not indicate electricity prices, investments, employment or effects on household budgets. It also does not specify which plants are located in the individual cantons. The directly documented impact is therefore informative: the statistics of the plants in operation are accompanied by an overview built on a historical reference and the existence of the plants.
This limit also counts for public communication. An article or a sheet that reports only the numerical threshold, without specifying whether it is initial or installed power, loses the central distinction of the ratio. A correct reading does not require adding estimates: it requires keeping exactly the criteria indicated.

Check, in order, the initial capacity of at least 10 kilowatts, operation in the reference year 1914 and the fact that the plant still exists. 4. Make the comparison only afterwards. If you consult the statistics on Switzerland's hydroelectric plants, note separately the threshold of at least 300 kilowatts of installed capacity and the criterion of plants in operation.

item.title: Parmelin resigns: the business community thanks him
item.description: The 66-year-old Federal Councillor Guy Parmelin announced his resignation today; Economiesuisse and the FSVO praise its agreements with India, Vietnam and renewal with China, as well as the Corporate Relief Act in force from 2024.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - Guy Parmelin announced his resignation today. - Economiesuisse and the FSV praised his economic achievement. - Agreements mentioned: India, Vietnam and the start of renewal with China. - The Business Relief Act has been in force since 2024.
## Key Facts - Decision → resignation announced today - Age → 66 years - Department → EAER - Agreements → India, Vietnam and start of renewal China - Business Relief Act, in force → 2024 - Training → Professional Bachelor and Professional Master - Date → October 1, 2026 - President of the USC → Markus Ritter
Federal Councillor Guy Parmelin's decision to resign, announced today, has also provoked reactions from the business world. Monika Rühl, Director of Economiesuisse, expressed regret for the choice and paid tribute to the 66-year-old's merits in the business world.
> Parmelin has worked tirelessly for a strong Switzerland as a business location.
According to Rühl, numerous free trade agreements of great importance to the exporting Confederation have been negotiated under her leadership. The director thanked Parmelin for the good cooperation.
Economiesuisse considers the commitment of the successor of the People's Party leader at the head of the EAER to be decisive for a competitive Swiss business location. From an economic point of view, Rühl stressed, the department must remain in bourgeois hands.
### Trade, business and training
The FSVO also expressed its appreciation for the departing Federal Councillor. In its financial statements, the association described Parmelin's work in economic policy as exceptional, with particular reference to the free trade agreements with India and Vietnam. It also attributed to Parmelin the initiation of the renewal of the free trade agreement with China.
Among the internal policy measures, the FSVO cited the law on the relief of companies, which came into force in 2024. It then referred to the revision of the vocational education and training legislation and the enhancement of tertiary level professional education and training through the additional titles Professional Bachelor and Professional Master, which came into force on 1 October 2026.
For the FSVO, Parmelin was a valuable partner in social partnership and took employers' demands seriously. As President of the Confederation, the association adds, he represented Switzerland successfully and with dignity.
### The USC Assessment
Markus Ritter, president of the Swiss Farmers' Union, praised Parmelin's leadership and ability to maintain calm and overview. He recalled the extraordinary challenges of the mandate: the coronavirus crisis, the war in Ukraine, the unpredictability of American trade policy over the past two years, the fire in Crans-Montana and the landslide in Blatten (VS). The Vaud politician, he added, was a crisis manager: with the Americans, he contributed to the search for solutions thanks to his French-speaking charm and convincing arguments, also choosing qualified personnel for his entourage. ## The point of operation for those who work
The clearest practical consequence concerns the succession at the helm of the EAER. In its reported reactions, Economiesuisse points to the competitiveness of Switzerland as a business location as a criterion for the successor. The source does not give the name of the future manager or describe an immediate measure for companies, employees or families: the step to be taken is therefore political and institutional, not a new individual procedure.
### Foreign trade as an indicator
The free trade agreements referred to by Economiesuisse and the FSVO define the foreign dossiers associated with Parmelin's budget. India and Vietnam are mentioned directly; for China, the source speaks of the start of the renewal, not of an agreement that has already been renewed. For exporting companies, this signals a political priority. However, it does not allow for the indication of sectors, costs, revenues, hires or deadlines: these data do not appear in the text.
Internally, the Business Relief Act and Vocational Education and Training have a distinct relevance. The former is referred to as a measure that came into force in 2024. The Professional Bachelor's and Professional Master's degrees, on the other hand, are presented as additional qualifications to tertiary level vocational education and training, which have been in force since 1 October 2026. The source does not specify requirements, costs, procedure or effects on employment contracts.
### Positions and decisions
The demand to keep the EAER in bourgeois hands is a position of Economiesuisse, not the name of a successor. Similarly, the FSVO's assessment of the social partnership describes the relationship it had with Parmelin and its focus on employers' demands; it does not announce new rules.
Markus Ritter's assessment adds the perspective of agriculture and crisis management: calm, oversight and the ability to deal with the Americans. Here, too, the source offers a judgment on the mandate, not a specific measure for farmers or the labor market.
To link this reading to your input, you can use the calcolatore stipendio/imposte: it is a separate tool and does not represent a change announced by the source.
## Recommended tools For an updated estimate, use the net salary calculator and the CHF-EUR exchange comparator. ## How to check the next steps
To use this news without overlapping different plans, it is worth proceeding by verification. The announcement of the resignation, the assessments of Economiesuisse, FSO and USC and the dossiers mentioned in Parmelin's financial statements do not have the same weight: the first concerns the announced decision, the second are judgments, the last are economic policy and education issues.
### A four-step checklist
1. Separate the dossiers. Classify the issue between free trade, business relief, vocational training, social partnership or crisis management. 2. Check the dates. The law is indicated as coming into force in 2024; for Professional Bachelor and Professional Master, the source indicates October 1, 2026. The announcement remains dated only as today. 3. Distinguish between positions and decisions. The Economiesuisse request on the EAER and the praise of the FSVO and FSO do not indicate the name of the successor or a new measure. 4. Limit conclusions. Don't add requirements, costs, industries, wage effects, or deadlines that the source doesn't specify.
An employer can thus understand whether his application concerns a business file, a measure for companies, higher education or social partnership. Those who study or work can mark the date of the additional qualifications, without attributing them conditions or advantages that are not described.
The source does not indicate forms, offices, applications to be submitted or documents to be prepared after the announcement. For this reason, the concrete step is to follow the evolution of the EAER and compare each subsequent communication with the facts already explained, without anticipating the appointment or the effects.
Those who follow agriculture can read the USC's judgment as an assessment of Parmelin's leadership, not as a new decision for the sector. The same criterion applies to the statements of the associations: check who is speaking, on which dossier and whether the text describes an event that has already happened or a request.
To orient yourself at work, annunci di lavoro and aziende che assumono remain available, tools separate from the political dossier. For personal income control, use calcolatore stipendio/imposte.

item.title: Health insurance: let's not call it a success
item.description: Premiums in Ticino +3.7% in 2027 compared to the Swiss average of 5%. The average premium reaches 519.90 francs, +56% in a decade.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief
- In 2027, Ticino's premiums will increase by 3.7%. - The Swiss average premium rate will rise by 5%. - The average Ticino premium will reach 519.90 francs per month. - In a decade, the Ticino premium has grown by about 56%.
## Key Facts
- Author → Luca Frasa, Movimento giovani leghisti - Year → 2027 - Increase in Ticino → 3.7% - Swiss average → 5% - Average Ticino premium → CHF 519.90 per month - Growth in the last decade → about 56% - Compared to Zug → around 11% - Proposal → uniform premiums at national level
In 2027, Ticino will see health insurance premiums increase by 3.7%, compared to 5% of the Swiss average. The Council of State speaks of an encouraging sign and the first effects of the work done. Luca Frasa, of the Young League Movement, however, urges not to read yet another price increase as a victory.
> "Let's take note of it. But let's not turn yet another increase into a victory."
### The figure beyond 2027
The average Ticino premium will rise to 519.90 francs per month, still the highest in Switzerland. The percentage expected for 2027 comes after years of price increases that, according to the author, have hit the canton harder than others. The message therefore does not only concern next year's change, but the path that preceded it.
In the last decade, the premium in Ticino has grown by about 56%. In other cantons the increase has been much lower; in Zug, for example, it is around 11%. The comparison shows the distance accumulated over time, without canceling the fact that the Ticino annual figure is lower than the expected Swiss average.
For Ticino families, writes Frasa, these are not abstract percentages. It is money that every month is added to rents, energy, shopping, mobility and a cost of living that continues to put pressure on purchasing power.
### The funding proposal
The issue is presented as structural. The KVG is federal and compulsory benefits are governed by the same law throughout Switzerland; however, financing through premiums produces enormous differences between one canton and another. In recent days, Frasa reports that he has coordinated with Alessandro Mazzoleni, deputy in the Grand Council of the Lega dei Ticinese.
Mazzoleni then presented a cantonal initiative to ask Bern for a modification of the KVG: uniform premiums at national level for the same age, deductible and insurance model, together with a national distribution of the costs of compulsory care. To accompany the public data with a verification of the insurance issue, confronto cassa malati e LAMal is available. ### How to Really Interpret the Increase
The first practical step is to distinguish the pace of the increase from its starting level. An increase below the national average is still an increase: it does not mean that the premium is decreasing or that the burden on the household budget will automatically be reduced. The news says that Ticino will grow less than the average in 2027; it also says that it starts from an already very high average level.
The second step is to separate a single year from the trajectory. A budget built only around the next adjustment risks overlooking the effect of previous years. The comparison with Zugo is precisely meant to show this trajectory: in Ticino, growth over the last decade was much more pronounced. The figure therefore raises a question about how spending is financed, not just about its immediate change.
| Reading perspective | What it means for a family | |---|---| | Annual increase | Measures the expected increase for 2027 | | Average premium | Provides a monthly reference for Ticino | | Ten-year evolution | Shows the cumulative effect of increases | | Comparison between cantons | Highlights regional differences | | Financing | Takes the debate beyond the percentage alone |
### From Premium to Monthly Spending
The source places the premium alongside rent, energy, groceries and transportation. Therefore, the practical interpretation does not consist in memorizing a percentage, but in checking how much room remains each month after these expenses. The cost of living is not presented as a separate item: it is the overall pressure on purchasing power.
The political issue concerns the structure. If mandatory benefits are regulated by the same LAMal throughout Switzerland, the place where a person lives still affects the bill through the premium mechanism. The proposal brought to Bern changes the perspective: not only how to slow increases, but how to finance a mandatory federal social insurance scheme.
The idea of uniform premiums for people with the same age, deductible and insurance model, with a national distribution of the costs of mandatory care, opens up a focused debate. The reader can separate two questions: how much the premium affects their budget today and what criterion should distribute the costs among the cantons. To organize the first part together with the other expenses, one can consult costo della vita in Svizzera.
## Useful tools to protect your net income To reduce FX leakage, compare CHF-EUR exchange options and banks for cross-border workers. ### An operational path to read shopping
A personal check can start from a monthly sheet built for 2027. There is no need to turn the national trend into a promise of savings: it is necessary to use it as a reference to read one's spending and the weight of the different items.
1. Set the horizon. Write 2027 at the top of the card and note the average Ticino premium indicated in the source as a parameter of comparison with your monthly invoice. 2. Separate expenses. Keep health insurance, rent, energy, spending and mobility on different lines so that you can see which costs are affecting your budget together. 3. Compare the levels. Record the expected increase for Ticino, the Swiss average and the evolution of the last decade without confusing the annual figure with the accumulated one. 4. Divide the two plans. On the one hand, place the expenditure that weighs today; on the other hand, note the discussion on the modification of the KVG and the financing criteria.
This method helps not to use the national comparison as an automatic response to the situation of each family. The average premium is a reference for Ticino, while the concrete pressure arises from the set of monthly expenditures. The sheet also allows you to check whether the increase is assessed alone or together with the rest of the cost of living.
In order to follow the political proposal, the points to be kept separate are those indicated in the cantonal initiative: uniform premiums at national level, age parity, deductible and insurance model, as well as the national distribution of the costs of compulsory care. In this way, the debate remains anchored in readable criteria and not just in the percentage of the year.
The verification can be updated when the 2027 framework is examined in the household budget. To turn this reading into an assessment of personal income and expenses, use the calcolatore stipendio.

item.title: ETH study: poor and rich pay the same taxes
item.description: Research by ETH Zurich reveals that almost everyone pays 45% of their income. Only the richest 1% pay less due to health premiums and VAT.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - The overall system amounts to approximately 45% of gross income. - Only the richest 1% pays a lower share. - Health insurance premiums and VAT weigh more heavily on lower incomes. - The ETH method includes taxes, transfers and government benefits.
## Key facts - Study → Swiss Federal Institute of Technology Zurich (ETH) - Researcher → Isabel Martinez, ETH KOF Institute - Overall share → approximately 45% of gross income - Bracket paying the least → richest 1% - Burdens mentioned → health insurance premiums and VAT - Method → overall national income, taxes, transfers and government benefits - Wealth → grows faster than incomes - Investments → stocks, including in the third pillar
Approximately 45% is the share of gross income that, according to the ETH study, is paid by all social groups. Only the richest 1% pays less. The research was presented by Isabel Martinez, a researcher at ETH Zurich's KOF Institute, in an interview published by Beobachter in its current issue. The news was reported by Keystone-ATS.
The point of the research is the gap between the progressivity envisaged for some taxes and the outcome of overall taxation. Income tax and, in part, wealth tax are structured progressively: those who earn more pay more. But, according to Martinez, health insurance premiums and VAT are left out of this initial view, independent of income and a heavier burden on lower-income groups. In the middle-income bracket, by contrast, employment income and the social contributions levied on it carry more weight. The issue of cassa malati premiums is therefore central to the explanation.
> «All social groups pay approximately 45% of their gross income: only the richest 1% pays less».
### Why the picture is broader When asked whether, despite the Federal Constitution, taxation is not based on ability to pay, the economist replies that this conclusion can be reached by looking at taxes and contributions together. The study did not consider only taxable income and wealth. It used total national income from the national accounts and included taxes, transfers and government benefits, calculating who receives what share before and after these levies and interventions.
The calculation includes supplementary benefits, pensions and health-insurance subsidies, but also undistributed corporate profits and tax-advantaged dividends intended for majority shareholders. For Martinez, including all these incomes makes the picture more precise and more unequal.
Finally, the study links growing inequality to wealth. In Switzerland, wealth grows faster than incomes, but the advantage goes to those who own wealth: those who do not own a home do not automatically benefit from rising property prices. Returns on wealth can then fuel further income inequality.
Martinez also urges caution regarding stocks. Investing savings, for example in the third pillar, has become easier, but understanding the market and choosing the right product is more difficult than comparing mortgages. This difficulty, she concludes, can create uncertainty and discourage. ## How to read the levy in the balance sheet
The ETH figure is not equivalent to the rate indicated on an individual return. It measures the share of national income that remains after the set of taxes, contributions and benefits, or that which is redistributed through state interventions. For a resident, the practical check must keep the levels of Swiss tax separate: direct federal tax, cantonal tax and municipal tax. Each canton has its own law and multiplier; the municipality applies its multiplier to the cantonal tax. The comparison between two budgets can therefore also change depending on the tax location.
### Entries not to be confused The table helps to reconstruct the transition from gross income to the overall burden:
| Voice | How it enters the reading | What to check | |---|---|---| | Income and wealth taxes | They are structured progressively | Portion paid in relation to income | | VAT | It is independent of income and is mainly levied on low incomes | Weight on expenditure | | KVG/KVG | Premiums are per capita, not a tax or a wage contribution | Cantonal premium and reduction | | Social contributions | Are levied on income from employment in the middle range | Deductions from wages | | State benefits | Includes pensions, supplementary benefits and health insurance benefits | Amounts received |
This distinction avoids confusing the progressivity of the tax with the cost of living. KVG/KVG premiums vary by canton and region, and the premium reduction is cantonal; for residents, insurance is compulsory. The source points to premiums as one of the reasons why the overall burden weighs relatively more heavily on low incomes, alongside VAT and social security contributions.
For those who work on a salary, the transition from gross to net also includes pension contributions such as AHV/AHV and BVP/BVG, while pension benefits enter the considered transfer side. For those who do not own real estate, the comparison changes again: rising property prices do not produce an automatic profit, while assets generate returns.
### The useful comparison The practical question is not only what tax is paid, but what items remain after deductions and what benefits are received. A balance sheet that records taxes, VAT, premiums, contributions and transfers offers a reading closer to the ETH method. To learn more about the territorial effect on costo della vita in Svizzera, it is advisable to keep the tax and health items separate.
## Useful planning tools To estimate your pension strategy, use the pension planner and the pillar 3 simulator. ## How to do a personal verification
The source does not propose a simulation for the individual taxpayer, but its method suggests a concrete sequence. The goal is not to look for a single rate: it is necessary to reconstruct gross income, separate withdrawals and benefits and distinguish assets from their returns. It is a broader reading than one based only on income or taxable assets.
### Four operational steps 1. Start with gross. Write down your earned income and any property income. Separate the pre-tax portion from the after-tax portion. If there are retained earnings or subsidized dividends, the research will look at them in the big picture.
2. Separate the tax authorities. Put direct federal tax, cantonal tax and municipal tax in different columns. The canton applies its own law and multiplier; the municipality uses the multiplier on the cantonal one. This avoids comparisons based on a single item.
3. Isolate health and consumption. Record the KVG/KVG premiums separately from VAT. For those residing in Switzerland, the KVG is mandatory and must be taken out within 3 months of arrival; the premiums are per person and depend on the canton and region. Also check the cantonal premium reduction, without treating it as a complete cancellation of the disparity described by the source.
4. Look at your assets. If you don't own real estate, don't automatically attribute rising house prices to you. If you evaluate stocks or the role of retirement provision, you can delve into AVS/LPP/rendita; don't turn the article into investment advice. Martinez warns that understanding the market and choosing the right product is more difficult than comparing mortgages. The third pillar is cited by the source as a possible area for investing savings, but caution remains necessary.
The final audit must put gross, taxes, VAT, premiums, contributions, benefits and assets side by side. This is how the comparison sticks to the method described and does not exchange a single deduction for the entire cost of living. To translate this data into a personal estimate, use the calcolatore stipendio.

item.title: Micasa changes ownership and closes four branches
item.description: Swiss investor group acquires 100% of Micasa; Crissier will close by the end of 2026 and Langendorf, Brügg, Buchs by January 2027. Operational management unchanged.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - A Swiss group acquires 100% of Micasa's shares - Four branches will close between the end of 2026 and January 2027 - Agustoni and Landolt remain at the operational helm - Micasa has been independent since September 1, 2025
## Key Facts - Owned → Swiss investor group - Stake acquired → 100% - Subsidiaries involved → Crissier, Langendorf, Brügg and Buchs - Deadlines → end of 2026 and end of January 2027 - Operational management → Philipp Agustoni and Manuel Landolt
### The transfer of ownership Micasa changes hands again: a group of Swiss investors has taken over 100% of the shares of the furniture retailer. The company announced the transaction on Friday to the AWP agency, confirming what was anticipated by Inside Paradeplatz. The names of the investors have not been disclosed.
However, the operational leadership remains in the hands of Philipp Agustoni, CEO, and Manuel Landolt, COO. According to the company, the new ownership will bring additional capital, entrepreneurial experience and expertise in the areas of logistics, digitalization and technology. The share change is therefore accompanied by a strengthening indicated by the company on specific operating areas, without changing the two main managers of management.
### The four locations involved The plan is to close four of the 30 Micasa branches. The Crissier site will permanently lower its shutters by the end of 2026. Langendorf, Brügg and Buchs will follow by the end of January 2027. The reason given by the company is the current economic situation and the changed market conditions.
Alternative solutions are being examined for the employees involved. The communication does not associate a different outcome for each location for the staff: the only element indicated is that the alternatives are still being examined. For customers, the calendar therefore distinguishes an initial deadline for Crissier and a subsequent one for the other three branches.
This is the second change of ownership in less than two years. In February 2025, Migros sold Micasa through a management buy-out to a consortium led by Agustoni and Landolt, with the participation of the German and Austrian investor families Brandstetter-Finger and Wiest. Since 1 September 2025, Micasa AG has been operating independently.
The company is active in the mid-price segment and compares itself on the market with Ikea and XXXLutz, among others. The new operation therefore changes the ownership of Micasa, while communication maintains the operational direction and declared positioning. ### A more concentrated network
The most readable operational data for those who use the points of sale is the concentration of the network: the communication concerns four out of 30 branches, not the entire brand. The difference between the deadlines counts. Crissier has the end of 2026 as its deadline; Langendorf, Brügg and Buchs follow by the end of January 2027. Those who have to deal with one of these locations must therefore start from the location, not from a single date valid for the whole of Micasa.
The transition must be read on two levels. On the one hand, there is the continuity of management: Agustoni and Landolt remain responsible for operations. On the other hand, the owner changes, with 100% of the shares acquired by a group of Swiss investors. The company links this new phase to additional capital, entrepreneurial experience and expertise in logistics, digitization and technology. These are the concrete elements indicated to accompany the management, while the communication does not present an additional timetable for the network.
| Plan | Given by Communication | Practical Reading | | Network | 30 branches, four closures | The announced consequences affect four locations | | Calendar | end of 2026 and end of January 2027 | there is no single deadline | | Management | CEO Philipp Agustoni and COO Manuel Landolt | The top management remains the same | | Ownership | 100% to Swiss investors | the change concerns the shareholding structure |
For the public, this avoids a too broad conclusion: the source does not announce the closure of the entire chain and does not present the four decisions as a plan extended to all locations. The reason given remains that of the current economic situation and changed market conditions. The comparison with Ikea and XXXLutz confirms the competitive terrain declared by Micasa, but does not offer elements to quantify prices, quotas or results.
The impact on the household budget therefore remains to be assessed without attributing effects to the new ownership that have not been announced. Micasa operates in the medium price segment: to frame this item of expenditure together with other domestic expenses, you can consult the costo della vita in Svizzera.
## Useful tools to protect your net income To reduce FX leakage, compare CHF-EUR exchange options and banks for cross-border workers. ### The dates to mark
To follow the story in a practical way, the verification can be organized in four steps:
1. Locate the location: check if the reference is Crissier, Langendorf, Brügg or Buchs. 2. Associate the correct deadline: Crissier by the end of 2026; Langendorf, Brügg and Buchs by the end of January 2027. 3. Separate the share plan from the operating one: the Swiss group has acquired 100%, but the management remains with Agustoni and Landolt. 4.
