## In brief - Federal Council launches consultation on 2 October 2026 - The procedure ends on January 19, 2027 - Switzerland signs the Protocol on 19 September 2025
## Key Facts - Subject: → Third Additional Protocol to the CEAG - Consultation → launched on 2 October 2026 - Deadline → 19 January 2027 - Swiss signature → Malta, 19 September 2025 - Ratification → Parliament
## The passage decided by the Federal Council
During its meeting on 2 October 2026, the Federal Council initiated the consultation procedure on the Third Additional Protocol to the European Convention on Mutual Assistance in Criminal Matters. The procedure will be completed on 19 January 2027. Switzerland has already signed the protocol: it was signed in Malta on 19 September 2025 at the informal conference of ministers of justice.
The European Convention on Mutual Assistance in Criminal Matters, or CEAG, is an agreement of the Council of Europe. Switzerland is a contracting party to it. Its structure links criminal cooperation to respect for individual rights: fair trial, proportionality of state interference and protection against arbitrariness.
### What does the CEAG govern?
The CEAG obliges the Contracting States to assist each other in cross-border criminal prosecution. Examples include the taking of evidence through the hearing of witnesses, experts or accused persons. The Convention also lays down the procedure and conditions for the submission and execution of letters rogatory.
The new protocol stems from the Council of Europe's objective of making the fight against cross-border crime more efficient, while maintaining compatibility with the rights of the accused. The Committee of Ministers of the Council of Europe adopted it before Switzerland's signature. In the communiqué, the Third Protocol is presented as a step in the modernisation and harmonisation of cross-border criminal prosecution in Europe.
Among the innovations mentioned is the possibility of transmitting letters rogatory electronically, taking into account technological developments in modern media. Switzerland contributed to the drafting of the text, in particular on the provisions relating to the cross-border use of technical recording devices, such as GPS trackers, and the surveillance of telecommunications traffic. Parliament will have the final say on ratification.
The timetable distinguishes between three institutional steps: the signature of the text by Switzerland, the start of the consultation by the Federal Council and the subsequent decision by Parliament on ratification. The consultation is therefore the step indicated by the Federal Council before the parliamentary decision. ## What changes on the operational level
In order to understand the scope of the dossier, it is necessary to separate what the CEAG already provides for from the additions to the Third Protocol. The Convention requires the Contracting States to assist each other in cross-border criminal prosecution and regulates the submission and execution of letters rogatory. The Protocol, on the other hand, focuses on the electronic transmission of requests and the adaptation of cooperation to modern means of communication.
### Three areas to observe
The first concerns evidence. The basic text provides for the hearing of witnesses, experts and defendants; the reader can therefore distinguish the content of the request from the way in which it is transmitted. The second concerns technology: the communiqué indicates new electronic possibilities for letters rogatory. The third includes provisions on the cross-border use of technical recording devices, including GPS trackers, and on the surveillance of telecommunications traffic.

## A handover with open files
On 29 November, Guy Parmelin will once again be called upon to defend the revised War Material Act before the people. In the meantime, his successor at the helm of the Federal Department of Economic Affairs, Education and Research, the EAER, will have to take charge of strategic dossiers for the future of Switzerland.
Among the challenges are the US tariffs. Switzerland has been negotiating with the United States on tariffs for exports to the American continent for months. Parmelin had taken it up again after the complicated start between Karin Keller-Sutter and President Trump. The declaration of intent signed in November 2025 aims to reduce the uncertainty of rates changed according to the mood of the US administration.
In free trade, Parmelin concluded agreements with India, renewed the agreement with China and continued the one with Mercosur. Parliament approved the South American treaty, but agricultural circles and those linked to the protection of the environment and human rights promised a referendum. The successor will have to defend it before the people.
### The Federal Economic Machine
The succession also concerns the State Secretariat for Economic Affairs. Helene Budliger Artieda, who will resign next March, played a crucial role in the trade negotiations. The Federal Council will have to appoint her successor; it is unclear whether Parmelin will be able to propose a candidate before leaving.
### Agriculture, arms and relations with the EU
Parmelin, a winegrower by profession, presented the agricultural policy for the coming years. The PA30+ provides for cuts in direct payments for small farms in the lowlands. Farmers and environmentalists are contesting the project, which the next person responsible will have to defend before parliament in 2028.
War material will be the focus of the vote on November 29. If the changes are rejected, the right will lobby for the Swiss arms industry; if they pass, the left will criticize the weight of economic interests on humanitarian law.
The Swiss-EU package is being examined by parliament. After discussions in the Council of States on wage protection, state aid and European research and education programmes, the National Council will address the issue in December: Parmelin will be able to defend the government's position, or it will be up to his successor.
### Houses and rentals
At the beginning of 2024, after two round tables with representatives from the cantons, cities, municipalities, construction and real estate, a national action plan with more than 30 measures was adopted. A follow-up is planned: the new head of the EAER is to find solutions to the housing shortage and rising rents and to deal with the Asloca initiative against high rents. item.description: The franc appreciates more than a cent in a day. Fears about European public debt and SNB rates at 0%.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - The franc rises by more than a cent against the euro in one day - The euro trades around 0.93 francs - Imports and travel cost less; exports suffer - SNB maintains key interest rate at 0%
## Key Facts - Strong appreciation → franc after months of weakness - Exchange rate → approx. 0.93 francs to one euro - Cause → weakness of the euro and fears about public debts - Effects → favored consumers, penalized exporting companies - Monetary policy → SNB policy rate at 0% from June 2025; unchanged on 24 September
### The movement of the franc After months of weakness, the franc reversed sharply and appreciated especially against the euro. In just one day, the rise exceeded one cent, a rare movement on the currency markets. In the morning, the euro was trading around 0.93 francs.
The Keystone-ATS agency attributes the strengthening mainly to the weakness of the euro. Concerns about the high debt of many eurozone states and the US have been with investors for weeks. New tensions over the French financial situation and political uncertainty around the hexagonal budget broke the camel's back.
The yield difference between French and German government bonds widened sharply, as investors sold European assets. In these phases, money traditionally flows into the franc, which is considered a safe haven.
### Switzerland as a refuge Commerzbank analysts point to Switzerland's debt brake, described as working, and a public debt that is not comparable to that of other industrialized countries.
> "In a world where bond yields are rising everywhere, there are no longer many markets to hide in," say Commerzbank analysts.
In addition to France's public finances, investors are looking at geopolitical tensions in the Middle East and energy price developments. The US dollar and the Japanese yen are also considered relatively defensive, but the yen is struggling, also due to the Bank of Japan's recent rate hikes.
The SNB, on the other hand, has maintained its key interest rate at 0% since June 2025 and left it unchanged on 24 September. In Switzerland, inflation remains within the framework of price stability and the economy is growing. The sale of European assets has thus strengthened the Swiss currency just as the market was once again seeking protection. ## The effect on the cost of living and exports A stronger franc is first and foremost good news for Swiss consumers. Foreign goods and services tend to cost less if companies pass on the exchange rate gain. The advantage concerns imported goods, travel abroad and purchases in eurozone countries. Energy and raw materials paid for in foreign currencies can also weigh less on prices in the Confederation. For the cost of living, the concrete check must be made on the final price, not just the quotation.
### From exchange to receipt The transfer is neither automatic nor complete. Traders and manufacturers may have bought months in advance, worked on long-term contracts or had exchange rate hedges. The change in price can therefore arrive later at retail and not transfer entirely. The comparatore CHF/EUR allows you to read the current price; however, it does not prove that a shop has already reduced the price.
| Area | Effect to be observed | |---|---| | Imported goods | Possible price reduction if exchange gain is passed on | | Travel and shopping in the Eurozone | Advantage for the Swiss consumer, linked to foreign currency | | Energy and raw materials | Possible price relief in the Confederation | | Exports & Tourism | "Swiss made" more expensive abroad; disadvantage for activities with costs in Swiss francs and foreign currency revenues |
For export-oriented companies, the opposite is the case. The strong franc makes "Swiss made" sold abroad more expensive, especially if the costs remain in Swiss francs and the revenues come in euros, dollars or other currencies. The price is therefore particularly relevant for industry and parts of tourism.
Companies can partially compensate for the disadvantage by acting on prices, productivity, by hedging foreign exchange or by means of production sites abroad. The same currency can relieve domestic prices and make it more difficult to sell outside Switzerland: the advantage for consumers and the pressure on exports go hand in hand.
## Useful tools to protect your net income To reduce FX leakage, compare CHF-EUR exchange options and banks for cross-border workers. ## How to turn the change into a decision Currency movements are best read by separating the price from the actual effect on the balance sheet. For a household or company, control can remain simple and focus on items exposed to foreign currency.
### Four steps for those who live in Switzerland 1. Identify the exposure: imported goods, foreign services, travel or purchases in Eurozone countries. For a company, separate costs in francs and revenues in euros, dollars or other currencies. 2. Compare the current price with the actual price in Swiss francs. The comparatore CHF/EUR helps you to read the exchange rate before considering a purchase. 3. Check airtime: months in advance, long-term contracts, and foreign exchange hedges can delay the effect on the price. 4. Update the valuation only on the price actually charged. A stronger franc does not mean that every foreign good or service costs less immediately and entirely.
To follow the impact on the costo della vita in Svizzera, it is worth starting with what you actually pay. If the price does not change, the favourable rate has not yet been transferred or the transfer has only been partial.
### A control for companies If you sell abroad, you should measure costs in Swiss francs and foreign currency revenues separately. You can then look at the levers that are already available: acting on prices, improving productivity, using hedging operations or using production sites abroad. These are partial answers and do not completely eliminate the disadvantage.
The same applies to the parts of tourism exposed to the exchange rate. The price must be observed in conjunction with the actual prices: for a consumer, this means comparing the foreign price with the price in Swiss francs. For a company, it means understanding in which items the currency creates pressure and in which response is practicable.
The SNB maintains the key interest rate at 0%, and inflation in Switzerland remains within price stability while the economy grows. Day-to-day control must therefore remain anchored in actual expenditure or revenues, not in a generic forecast. item.description: Effective January 1, 2027, the law and the ordinance on the supervision and transparency of wholesale energy markets (OVTE) will take effect. ElCom will receive data on transactions and orders.
item.content:encoded:
## At a Glance - October 2, 2026: The Federal Council approves the OVTE - The law and ordinance take effect on January 1, 2027 - ElCom will receive transactions, orders, reports, and key data - REMIT and ACER guide uniform implementation
## Key Facts - What: OVTE Ordinance - Decision: Federal Council, October 2, 2026 - Legal basis: LVTE, adopted by Parliament in March 2025 - Effective date: January 1, 2027 - Authority: Federal Electricity Commission (ElCom) - Threshold: annual consumption capacity exceeding 600 gigawatt-hours - Standard: EU REMIT Regulation - Guidelines: ACER
On October 2, 2026, in Bern, the Federal Council approved the Ordinance on Supervision and Transparency in Wholesale Energy Markets (OVTE). The ordinance contains the implementing provisions for the Federal Act on Supervision and Transparency in Wholesale Energy Markets (LVTE), which was adopted by Parliament in March 2025.
Both the Act and the Ordinance will enter into force on January 1, 2027. The OVTE establishes the technical and procedural arrangements necessary to implement the rules on transparency and supervision in wholesale energy markets in Switzerland.
### Procedures Set Forth in the Ordinance
The text regulates the registration of market participants with the Federal Electricity Commission (ElCom), the publication of inside information, and the reporting of transactions, trading orders, positions, and key data to the authority. The ordinance thus defines the steps for making the required information public and for reporting it to ElCom.
It also sets forth procedures for authorizing platforms used for the publication of inside information and for reporting mechanisms. The text further specifies details regarding the use of inside information, market practices, and the collection of fees by ElCom in connection with its supervisory activities.
The scope includes companies active in the trade of electricity and natural gas, both on the European and Swiss markets. The new regulations also apply to Swissgrid, natural gas transmission system operators, operators of distribution networks or electricity or natural gas storage facilities, producers, intermediaries, suppliers, balance group managers, and large end consumers with an annual consumption exceeding 600 gigawatt-hours.
To reduce the administrative burden and promote uniform application, the OVTE is largely based on the European standards set forth in the EU Regulation on the Integrity and Transparency of the Wholesale Energy Market, known as REMIT. ElCom will provide practical guidance based on the guidelines of the EU Agency for the Cooperation of Energy Regulators (ACER). The transitional provisions call for a phased introduction and allow market participants time to adapt their systems and processes. For a separate in-depth analysis of daily expenses in Switzerland, see costo della vita in Svizzera. ## Operational Implications
The practical implications of the OVTE focus on operators’ processes. The source identifies a broad range of stakeholders: from companies that trade electricity and gas to Swissgrid, network and storage operators, producers, intermediaries, suppliers, and large end-users. For the latter, the specified criterion is an annual consumption capacity exceeding 600 gigawatt-hours.
The press release does not assign a separate obligation to each category, but rather outlines which activities fall within the scope of the new regulations. The operational overview can be interpreted as follows:
| Entity or Area | Operational Point | |---|---| | Market participants | Registration procedure with ElCom | | Inside information | Publication in accordance with the prescribed procedure | | Transactions and orders | Transmission to ElCom of transactions, orders, positions, and key data | | Trading platforms | Authorization for publication and reporting mechanisms | | Supervision | Rules on inside information, market practices, and remuneration |
### The Transition from Preparation to Implementation
The “before and after” comparison has a fixed date: January 1, 2027. Until that date, transitional provisions give affected parties time to adapt their systems and processes. After the regulations take effect, the framework will include technical and procedural requirements defined by the OVTE, with a phased introduction of the new obligations.
This approach aims to prevent each company from developing its own operational model. The reference to the European standards of the REMIT Regulation serves to facilitate implementation and minimize the administrative burden as much as possible. The practical guidelines that ElCom will provide, based on ACER’s guidelines, are intended to support uniform implementation.
The national context is therefore particularly relevant for operators active in wholesale energy markets or those providing relevant data and infrastructure. For other categories, the document does not outline specific procedures. Those interested in the corporate side of the Swiss market may supplement this reading with aziende che assumono.
## Useful tools to protect your net income To reduce FX leakage, compare CHF-EUR exchange options and banks for cross-border workers. ## What to Prepare Before the Ordinance Takes Effect
Those operating in one of the specified categories can translate the new ordinance into an action plan even before January 1, 2027. The procedure is not the same for everyone: it depends on the role played in the market and the data processed. However, the text of the source allows us to identify five operational checks.
### Five Operational Checks
1. Identify your role. You must determine whether your activity falls under market operators, trading companies, network or storage operators, producers, intermediaries, suppliers, balance group managers, or large end consumers.
2. Verify the registration process. For market participants, the OVTE regulates registration with ElCom. The first step is therefore to follow the procedure specified by the authority.
3. Map out the information. Internal systems and processes must account for inside information, transactions, trading orders, exposures, and fundamental data—that is, the elements that the new regulations link to reporting or disclosure.
4. Review platforms and reporting mechanisms. Affected companies must examine the procedures for authorizing platforms to publish inside information and for reporting mechanisms.
5. Plan for compliance. The transitional provisions call for a phased implementation. The internal timeline must therefore account for the effective date of January 1, 2027, and the practical instructions that ElCom will provide based on ACER guidelines.
For large end consumers, the threshold to verify is an annual consumption capacity exceeding 600 gigawatt-hours. For all other entities, the priority is to align their role with the procedures outlined in the ordinance, without anticipating requirements not specified in the source.
Preparations should focus on systems and processes, as provided for in the transitional provisions, and keep publication, transmission, and reporting obligations separate. To link the economic framework to personal income, try calcolatore stipendio.

item.title: Parmelin Leaves the Government: Race to Succeed Him in the SVP
item.description: Guy Parmelin announced his resignation from the government on October 2, 2026; the SVP succession race closes on October 23, with the election scheduled for December 9, 2026.
item.content:encoded:
## At a Glance - Parmelin is leaving the government - The deadline to file for candidacy is October 23 - His successor will be elected on December 9 - The seat is expected to remain with the SVP
## Key Facts - Key figure → Guy Parmelin - Party expected to win the seat → SVP - Deadline to declare candidacy → October 23 - Election → December 9 - Economic Department → DEFR
In a statement on October 2, 2026, Guy Parmelin announced his resignation from the government. His departure kicks off the race for his successor, which will go to a vote in December during the winter session of Parliament. The election is scheduled for December 9. The contest will therefore play out among the candidates, the federal departments, and Parliament.
The seat is expected to remain with the SVP, Switzerland’s largest party. The Center, in two posts shared on X, acknowledged the SVP’s right to retain its two seats on the Federal Council. The PLR, on the other hand, expressed the hope that, for the succession to the Vaud representative, the party would consider candidates from French-speaking Switzerland.
### The Internal Struggle Within the SVP
Albert Rösti already holds one of the two SVP seats. Parmelin’s presence in the government represented the SVP’s expansion from German-speaking Switzerland to French-speaking Switzerland and Ticino. Now the balance between a Federal Councilor from German-speaking Switzerland and one from French-speaking Switzerland is back at the center of the debate.
A few minutes after the announcement, the Zurich SVP chapter stated that it intends to consider fielding its own candidate. The chapter is described as the party’s most influential; among the names mentioned in the past is SVP State Councilor Natalie Rickli. National Councilors Thomas Aeschi and Céline Amaudruz have also been mentioned.
The succession is intertwined with a possible reshuffling of the departments. Beat Jans, the Socialist from Basel, could set his sights on the Department of Economic Affairs—currently led by Parmelin—while the source points to previous shifts between the departments of Justice and Police, and the Department of Home Affairs and Finance, which involved Jans and Karin Keller-Sutter.
The DEFR leaves open the agreements with the EU—approved by the Council of States but still pending in the National Council—trade negotiations with the United States following the Trump administration’s tariffs on Swiss exports, and issues related to agricultural policy and free trade. Candidates have until October 23 to apply; this will be followed by hearings, proposals from the selection committee, and a final decision by the parliamentary caucus. The winner will become the 124th member of the Federal Council in history. The potential succession at the helm of the DEFR should not be interpreted as a decision that has already been made regarding economic issues. The source highlights open questions, not their outcome: for those who live or work in Switzerland, the concrete reality is therefore the institutional timeline and the stage each matter has reached. No specific amounts or immediate measures for families are announced; automatically linking Parmelin’s resignation to an impact on personal finances would go beyond the text.
| Issue | Status indicated in the source | What to watch | |---|---|---| | Agreements with the EU | Approved by the Council of States, but still to be submitted to the National Council | The next parliamentary step | | United States | Delicate trade negotiations following tariffs on Swiss exports | The approach of the next official in charge | | Agricultural policy | The future of the policy remains open | The DEFR’s priorities | | Free trade | The issue has sparked discontent in various circles | How it will be handled moving forward |
This distinction avoids two sources of confusion. The first is mistaking approval by the Cantonal Councils for a definitive green light for the agreements with the EU: the source still points to the hurdle of the National Council. The second is considering the trade policy toward the United States already settled: the talk is of delicate negotiations, not of a concluded agreement.
### Three Scenarios to Keep Separate
The first concerns internal representation. A potential candidacy from the Zurich SVP would bring the question of the balance between German-speaking and French-speaking Switzerland back to the forefront. A candidate from the French-speaking region would make the wish expressed by the PLR a current issue. Neither of these two possibilities is presented as a decision that has already been made.
The second scenario concerns Beat Jans. If he were to aim for the Department of Economic Affairs, it would trigger a new reshuffling of departments; however, the source does not indicate what the final structure would be. The third scenario concerns the policy dossiers: the new head of the DEFR would inherit unresolved issues, but the text does not anticipate a solution regarding agreements with the EU, trade negotiations, agriculture, or free trade.
To supplement this institutional analysis with a separate review of the personal budget, you can consult costo della vita in Svizzera and, without attributing those data to the source, calcolatore stipendio/imposte.
## Recommended tools For an updated estimate, use the net salary calculator and the CHF-EUR exchange comparator. ### Operational Timeline
The procedure outlined by the UDC allows one to follow the process step by step, without confusing a name that has been mentioned with a formal candidacy. For the reader, the key is to note the deadlines and distinguish between those who propose and those who decide.
1. By October 23. This is the window set by the UDC for interested parties who wish to come forward. Until that time, the names mentioned remain part of the race, not the final outcome.
2. After the deadline. The process of candidate hearings begins. This is the step that precedes the selection committee’s proposals and allows for a distinction between the hearing phase and the final political decision.
3. Proposal phase. The selection committee formulates its proposals. The final say rests with the parliamentary caucus, which decides which candidate—or candidates—to field.
4. December 9. The election of the successor takes place. Whoever wins the support of Parliament becomes the 124th member in history of the Federal Council.
In the meantime, the reader can create a two-column checklist: the date of the procedure and the decision that was actually reached. The first row should list the October 23 deadline; the second, the start of the hearings; the third, the committee’s recommendations and the parliamentary group’s choice; and the last, the December 9 vote. This outline helps ensure you don’t jump from one evaluated candidacy to a final outcome.
After the vote, the next step involves reviewing the departmental structure: the source suggests the possibility of Beat Jans moving to the Department of Economic Affairs and, consequently, a reshuffling of portfolios. Only then will it be possible to assess the new appointment alongside the DEFR’s ongoing initiatives, without anticipating decisions that have not yet been announced.

item.description: The Federal Council Adopts the Report on October 2, 2026: Five Priorities for Streamlining Procedures and Reducing Wait Times.
item.content:encoded:
## At a Glance - Report adopted by the Federal Council on October 2, 2026 - Five priority areas for automation and AI - Simpler, more practical procedures processed more quickly - First phase focused on an overview of federal systems
## Key Facts - Decision → Adoption of the report - Date → October 2, 2026 - Authority → Federal Council - Scope → Federal Administration - Priorities → Five areas of application
On October 2, 2026, in Bern, the Federal Council adopted the report “Increasing the Efficiency of Administrative Processes through Process Automation and Artificial Intelligence (AI),” in fulfillment of Postulate 24.3582 Silberschmidt. The document sets out guidelines for a more efficient use of process automation and AI within the Federal Administration.
The goal is to simplify procedures, speed up the processing of applications and cases, and make more effective use of available resources. The report assigns these technologies a central role in the fulfillment of tasks: they should reduce administrative burdens, improve quality, and free up resources for more important tasks.
This push stems from demographic changes and the increasing volume of data. The Federal Administration will have to carry out the same or an increasing number of tasks with more limited human resources.
### The Federal Vision
The Federal Council identifies automation and artificial intelligence as strategic digital resources for fulfilling legal mandates in an effective, efficient, and resilient manner. Automation should optimize processes and performance, support managers and staff, and pave the way for new solutions. However, the approach remains people-centered, reliable, and sustainable.
The five priorities are business management, with integrated and transparent processes; technology-assisted translation; the review of applications and cases, to reduce wait times and accelerate decision-making; data processing, through extraction, standardization, and harmonization; and business support processes, which also address the monitoring of financial transactions and procurement. For back-office operations, the report also mentions verifying the contractual basis, budget compliance, and internal regulations.
The report therefore envisages an initial internal phase: improving the overall view of the systems developed, purchased, or used by the Confederation; accelerating synergies between solutions; and promoting their large-scale implementation. Resources must be used sparingly and focused on cases with high scalability potential. ## Practical Impact on the Population and the Economy
The report outlines a course of action for the Federal Administration: to streamline the internal processes involved in handling applications and cases. For those who live or work in Switzerland, the potential benefit described is therefore linked to the quality and speed of their interactions with the Federal Administration.
### From Application to Decision
The most concrete result highlighted in the report concerns processing times. If automation is applied to the review of applications and cases, it should help reduce wait times and speed up the decision-making process. The wording describes an objective: the potential benefit should be understood as a path toward improvement, not as a result already achieved for every individual or business.
Integrated case management can impact the continuity of the process and the transparency of the steps between offices. The report refers to a process that extends from the submission of a parliamentary motion to its implementation. The same logic of integration is linked to common solutions for translation: the expected effect is to simplify processes and support the multilingualism of the Federal Administration.
Another effect concerns the information infrastructure. Data extraction, standardization, and harmonization must create a reliable foundation for dependable automation. The stated goal is therefore to prepare more consistent data for automated processes; the press release does not provide figures or results that have already been achieved.
For the back office, the impact primarily concerns business support processes: the verification of financial transactions and purchases can be standardized and accelerated, taking into account accuracy, contractual basis, budget, and internal regulations. The decision to focus resources on scalable cases indicates that the rollout will prioritize solutions with greater scalability. Readers interested in exploring this topic in relation to economic analysis can consult costo della vita in Svizzera for a separate in-depth analysis.
Finally, the framework sets a clear limit on the pursuit of speed alone: automation and AI must support managers and staff, remain people-centered, reliable, and sustainable. According to the report, administrative efficiency therefore encompasses timeliness, quality, resilience, and the prudent use of resources.

The press release focuses on the guidelines and the initial internal phase. To follow the implementation without adding details not contained in the source, it is best to read the report as a roadmap of the processes that the Confederation intends to make more efficient.
### Four Steps to Follow the Issue
1. Identify the type of process involved. The source distinguishes between case management, translation, review of applications and files, data processing, and business support. This classification helps clarify which outcome is being pursued.
2. If the topic is an application or a case, focus on the two indicators mentioned in the report: wait times and decision speed. These are the expected effects of automation; the text does not provide a one-size-fits-all deadline or a specific number of days to expect.

4. The first phase remains internal to the Confederation. It includes an overview of the AI and automation systems that have been developed, purchased, or are in use, as well as the acceleration of synergies and large-scale implementation. The stated criterion is frugality: resources should be concentrated on applications with high scalability potential.

item.description: In the first nine months, there were 11,412 bankruptcies in Switzerland, up 37% from 2025. Ticino and Graubünden were above average; 40,487 new companies were established.
item.content:encoded:
## At a Glance - 11,412 bankruptcies in the first nine months - +37% compared to the same period in 2025 - Construction: 1,380 companies, +13% - Ticino: 721 bankruptcies, +48%
## Key Facts - Source → Crif - Period → January–September - Change → as of January 1, 2025 - New companies → 40,487, +2%
In the first nine months of the year, there were 11,412 bankruptcies in Switzerland, 37% more than in the same period of 2025. The report bears the ATS acronym, in the form Keystone-ATS, and is based on data published by Crif, a company active in anti-fraud measures, credit checks, and information services for businesses and individuals.
### The Hardest-Hit Sectors The construction sector saw 1,380 affected companies, representing a 13% increase. This is followed by the restaurant industry, with 1,019 businesses and a 20% increase, and retail trade, with 895 businesses and a 51% increase. The sectoral breakdown thus highlights three distinct areas, though the source does not provide further explanations regarding individual companies.
At the regional level, Ticino and Graubünden show variations above the national average: in Ticino, there were 721 bankruptcies, a 48% increase, while in Graubünden the number reached 218, a 95% increase. In absolute terms, the highest numbers were recorded in Zurich, with 1,850 bankruptcies and a 28% increase; in Geneva, with 1,369 and a 65% increase; and in Vaud, with 1,006 and a 30% increase.
Crif also reports a shift in new business activity. Between January and September, 40,487 new companies were established, a 2% increase year-over-year. Business consulting leads this segment with 3,499 new companies and a 25% increase; followed by real estate, with 3,032 (+6%), construction, with 2,896 (+5%), and retail trade, with 2,823 new businesses (-12%). In Ticino, there were 1,806 new businesses, up 9%; in Graubünden, 853, up 8.1%.
The rise in bankruptcies also has a regulatory component. Starting January 1, 2025, tax debts owed by companies listed in the commercial register can be enforced through bankruptcy proceedings. Previously, authorities could collect unpaid taxes only through seizure. ## How to Interpret the Data
The national figure alone does not reflect the situation of each individual company. The source provides data on bankruptcy proceedings, percentage changes, sectors, and cantons, but does not indicate the amount of debt, the number of employees involved, or the outcome of individual cases. The practical distinction is between absolute figures and percentage changes: one canton may have fewer cases but a more pronounced increase, while another may have a higher concentration of bankruptcies without exceeding the national average.
### The Tax Change Alters the Interpretation The reference to January 1, 2025, prevents the +37% figure from being treated as a pure measure of economic performance. Crif cites the legislative change as one of the reasons for the increase, not as the sole explanation. Starting in 2025, for companies listed in the commercial register, tax debt may be included in bankruptcy proceedings; previously, the collection of unpaid taxes was limited to seizure of assets. The source thus describes a change in the collection channel but does not specify new tax amounts or rates.
The term “tax debts” remains general. The report does not distinguish between direct federal tax, VAT, and cantonal or municipal taxes, nor does it indicate which tax authority initiated the individual cases. The statistical source must also be distinguished. These figures are published by Crif: they are not presented as a series from SECO, UST/BFS, or BNS/SNB. The available data comes from a company active in credit checks and providing information to businesses and individuals. Geographically, the comparison remains limited to cantons and regions, with no municipal data or a complete ranking.

For a company, an employee, or anyone observing the cantonal market, the most prudent approach begins with five checks. These are not a failure-proof procedure; they are a way to avoid misinterpreting the available information.

1. Define the time period. The comparison covers January through September and measures bankruptcies relative to the same period in 2025. Do not automatically extrapolate the data to the entire year.
2. Identify the scope. Note the sector in question: construction, food service, or retail for bankruptcies; business consulting, real estate, construction, or retail for new companies. The trends vary by category.
3. Break down by region and size. For the canton in question, note both the absolute number and the percentage. A comparison between Ticino, Graubünden, Zurich, Geneva, and Vaud should not be interpreted based on a single indicator.
4. Verify the legal status. If the company is registered in the commercial register, note that as of January 1, 2025, tax debts may be enforced through bankruptcy proceedings. The source does not specify minimum amounts, additional deadlines, or required documentation.

item.description: Guy Parmelin to step down at the end of the year. The Center acknowledges the two SVP seats; the PLR calls for candidates from French-speaking Switzerland.
item.content:encoded:
## At a Glance - Parmelin will leave the Federal Council at the end of the year. - The Center Party has allocated two seats in the government to the SVP. - The PLR is also calling for candidates from French-speaking Switzerland. - USAM and Economiesuisse acknowledge the economic merits.
## Key Facts - Decision → Guy Parmelin’s resignation - Deadline → end of the year - SVP seats → two in the Federal Council - Candidates sought by the PLR → figures from French-speaking Switzerland - Agreements mentioned → India, Vietnam, and renewal with China - Business Relief Act → takes effect in 2024 - Professional degrees → Professional Bachelor’s and Professional Master’s degrees starting October 1, 2026
### A Succession That’s Already Political
BERN — Guy Parmelin, President of the Confederation and Federal Councilor, has announced his resignation, scheduled for the end of the year. The decision opens a debate on the profile of his successor and on how the Federal Council should address Switzerland’s current and future challenges.
The Center Party responded by acknowledging the SVP’s right to retain its two seats on the Federal Council. In the same statement, the party linked the succession to a specific political demand: the new member of the government must contribute to constructive cooperation, thereby enabling the executive branch to address the country’s challenges.
> The Center acknowledges the SVP’s claim to two seats on the Federal Council.
The SVP paid tribute to Parmelin for his long-standing commitment and expressed regret over his resignation. In its statement, the party noted that, as defense minister, Parmelin initially championed the strengthening of the armed forces and national defense. In the Department of Economic Affairs, the SVP continued, he strengthened Switzerland’s economic, educational, and research sectors.
The statement also highlights his commitment to open markets and favorable framework conditions. According to the SVP, Switzerland has improved, diversified, and expanded its trade relations. The party believes this policy facilitates companies’ access to growing markets, protects jobs, and strengthens the country’s prosperity.
The PLR, in turn, thanked the Federal Councilor for his many years of service and expressed an expectation to the UDC: the list of potential successors should also include figures from French-speaking Switzerland. This request is motivated by the country’s quadrilingual character and national cohesion.
Business associations emphasized the Department of Economic Affairs’ budget. The USAM praised the free trade agreements with India, Vietnam, and other countries, as well as the start of negotiations to renew the agreement with China. It also cited the Business Relief Act, the revision of the Vocational Training Act, and the Professional Bachelor’s and Professional Master’s degrees, which will take effect on October 1, 2026. item.title: New Car Sales in Switzerland: The Electric Vehicle Boom
item.description: In September, 202,900 new cars were sold in Switzerland, up 9.6% year-over-year. Electric vehicles accounted for 36% of the market, while alternative-fuel vehicles accounted for 79%.
item.content:encoded:
## At a Glance - September: 21,900 new cars, up 9.6% from the previous year - Alternative-fuel vehicles account for 79% of the market - Electric vehicles rise to 36%, with 7,800 cars sold - In the first nine months of 2026, 173,500 cars were sold, up 2.7%
## Key Facts - Period → September - Registrations → 21,900 new cars - Year-over-year growth → 9.6% - Alternative powertrains → 79% market share - Electric → 36%, with 7,800 electric cars - January–September 2026 → 173,500 cars - Growth over the first nine months → 2.7% - 4×4 → 53%, up from 50%
21,900 brand-new cars were put into service in Switzerland in September, 9.6% more than during the same slow period last year. The figure comes from the importers’ association Auto-Switzerland, as reported by Keystone-ATS.
### Drive Systems This Month In the ninth month of the year, alternative drive systems accounted for 79% of the market share, compared to 73% in September 2025. Electric vehicles led the way with 36%, up from 26% a year earlier: 7,800 electric cars were sold. Conventional hybrids followed at 32%, down from 34%, while plug-in hybrids accounted for 12%, remaining nearly stable compared to 13%. Gasoline-powered cars accounted for 17%, down from 22%, and diesel cars for 4%, down from 6%.
Total sales for the first nine months of 2026 rose to 173,500 vehicles, an increase of 2.7% year-over-year. In terms of volume, dealerships sold 62,600 hybrids (+2%), 45,500 electric vehicles (+27%), 34,900 gasoline-powered cars (-16%), 21,300 plug-in hybrids (+15%), and 9,300 diesel vehicles (-24%). The share of 4x4s rose from 50% to 53%.
### A Message from Auto-Switzerland > “The continued increase in electric vehicle registrations recorded in September is encouraging,” comments Thomas Rücker, director of Auto-Switzerland.
In the same statement, Rücker highlights the heavy financial burden on commuters and the transportation sector. The public and businesses, he argues, must not be left to fend for themselves: mobility costs must be significantly reduced. The director adds that the adoption of electric mobility remains a quarter below the projections in the federal government’s plans and calls for a rapid improvement in the regulatory framework. To relate this issue to daily expenses, refer to costo della vita in Svizzera, without attributing individual amounts to the source that it does not report. ## What the Numbers Tell Us The monthly figure and the cumulative total reflect two different perspectives. The 36% share indicates the proportion of electric vehicles among new registrations in September; while the 45,500 electric vehicles sold in the first nine months measure the cumulative volume over the same period. Distinguishing between these two indicators prevents confusion between the market composition in a single month and the partial annual total.
Even the 79% figure for alternative powertrains requires a nuanced interpretation. This share includes electric, conventional hybrid, and plug-in hybrid vehicles. The headline about the growth of electric cars therefore does not reflect the complete picture of alternative powertrains: the source presents three distinct categories, each showing a different trend. Gasoline and diesel are on separate trajectories, while the share of 4×4s rose from 50% to 53%.
### Competition Among Brands The manufacturer rankings add another criterion for comparison, again based on the first nine months. Volkswagen leads with 18,900 cars sold, ahead of Skoda with 16,000. Next are BMW with 13,900, Mercedes with 14,200, Audi with 11,600, and Toyota with 10,000. Further down the list are Seat/Cupra with 6,600 cars, Volvo with 6,500, Renault with 6,200, Dacia with 5,500, Tesla with 5,300, and Hyundai with 5,100.
BYD and KIA both reached 4,600 vehicles. Peugeot stands at 3,800, Ford at 3,600, MG at 3,500, and Porsche at 3,200; all other manufacturers fall short of 3,000 vehicles. This is a ranking of individual brands, not a ranking of electric cars alone.
For those who live or work in Switzerland, the most tangible impact relates to mobility expenses. Auto-Svizzera links the trend in registrations to the financial burden on commuters and transportation, but the text does not provide a cost per individual model or per person. It is therefore not possible to automatically equate the growth in electric vehicles with personal savings. To put the data in relation to one’s own income, readers can compare it with the busta paga svizzera, keeping the source figures separate from individual assessments.
## Recommended tools For an updated estimate, use the net salary calculator and the CHF-EUR exchange comparator. ## A Checklist for Using Data Correctly The source allows for a structured comparison across months, cumulative periods, vehicle types, and brands. This method ensures that market shares, absolute volumes, and year-over-year changes are not conflated, nor are sales statistics misrepresented as promises of savings.
### Five Steps 1. Define the period. For the monthly snapshot, start with the 21,900 cars registered in September and the 9.6% change compared to the same slow period the previous year. For a broader comparison, look at the first nine months of 2026.
2. Separate market share from volume. First, examine the market composition: 79% of vehicles use alternative powertrains, with individual shares for electric, conventional hybrid, plug-in hybrid, gasoline, and diesel. Then examine the cumulative volumes, without combining metrics based on different time periods.
3. Check the trends. The nine-month total is 173,500 cars, up 2.7%. The absolute figures are rounded to the nearest hundred, as the source specifies: the comparison should therefore be presented exactly as published.
4. Examine the market profile. The share of 4x4s rose from 50% to 53%, while the brand rankings show Volkswagen ahead of Skoda and other manufacturers. This step completes the analysis without confusing brand and powertrain type.
5. Relate the data to your own situation. Auto-Svizzera’s message concerns the financial burden on commuters, the general population, businesses, and the transportation sector. However, the source does not allow you to determine a personal expense or an automatic savings amount: to complete the analysis of disposable income, use calcolatore stipendio/imposte.

item.title: Fall Session: Mercosur, UBS Act & Bilaterals III
item.description: The Federal Chambers conclude their fall session. Green light for the Bilateral Agreements III, the Mercosur agreement, and the UBS Act.
item.content:encoded:
## At a Glance - The Council of States approves the decrees on Bilateral Agreements III - Bilateral Agreements III: mandatory vote and double majority - Lex UBS: 90% CET1 coverage for UBS - Hotel VAT at 3.8% through 2031
## Key Facts - Session → fall session, concluded with final votes - Bilateral Agreements III → mandatory vote and double majority of the people and the cantons - Lex UBS → 90% CET1 capital coverage for UBS - Hotel VAT → reduced rate of 3.8% through 2031 - Mercosur → Argentina, Brazil, Paraguay, and Uruguay
After 24 hours of debates spread over six days, the Federal Chambers closed the fall session today with final votes. ATS reports that among the approved measures are the roundtable for Crans-Montana, the agreement with Mercosur, and the passage of the so-called Bilateral Agreements III.
The Council of States approved all federal decrees in the package of agreements with the EU. The most significant decision concerns the mandatory vote on the Bilateral Agreements III: a double majority of the people and the cantons will be required. The measure now moves to the National Council, which has yet to vote on it.
### Banks, VAT, and Trade Agreements
The bill known as the “Lex UBS,” however, has been initiated but not finalized. The Council of States decided, despite opposition from UBS, that the bank must ensure 90% coverage with Common Equity Tier 1 (CET1) capital for the foreign holdings of systemic banks.
The provisions regarding VAT also remain unresolved. The Council of States has proposed a 0.2 percentage point increase to fund the military through 2045, but the measure has yet to be confirmed by the other chamber. The two chambers, however, decided to extend the reduced VAT rate for the hotel sector—currently at 3.8%—until 2031.
On foreign trade, Parliament adopted the free trade agreement between the EFTA states—including Switzerland—and Mercosur, comprising Argentina, Brazil, Paraguay, and Uruguay. Civil society organizations active in environmental protection and human rights have already announced a referendum.
Regarding Crans-Montana, the Chambers reached an agreement on the law authorizing the Confederation to contribute 20 million francs to the roundtable established following the New Year’s Eve fire. The solidarity contribution of 50,000 francs for each victim—in a fire that claimed 41 lives and left over 100 injured—had already been approved in March. ## A Practical Guide to Legislative Dossiers
Not all approvals carry the same procedural weight. To follow the session, it is helpful to distinguish between decisions adopted by the two chambers, proposals still pending, and dossiers put to a popular vote. This distinction clarifies what has already been decided and what remains to be addressed.
### An overview of the status of legislative proposals
| Proposal | Status as indicated by the session | |---|---| | Bilateral Agreements III | Decrees approved by the Council of States; forwarded to the National Council | | VAT increase for the military | 0.2 percentage points through 2045 proposed by the Council of States; awaiting action by the other chamber | | Hotel tax rate | Extension decided by both chambers through 2031 | | Mercosur | Agreement adopted; referendum announced | | Lex UBS | 90% coverage decided by the Council of States; bill not finalized |
The mandatory referendum on Bilateral Agreements III makes the parliamentary phase just one of several key stages: the National Council has yet to vote, and the final decision will require a double majority of the people and the cantons. For those who follow federal politics, the parliamentary process and the popular vote are therefore two distinct stages.
Mercosur is following a different path. Parliament has adopted the agreement, but civil society organizations have announced a referendum, and sources indicate that the final say should rest with the people. Parliamentary adoption, therefore, does not mark the end of the process.
On the VAT front, the two issues should not be lumped together. The 0.2-point increase to fund the military remains a proposal from the Council of States and is awaiting consideration by the other chamber. The extension of the reduced hotel tax rate, on the other hand, has been approved by both chambers of Parliament, with a term running through 2031. For the hotel sector, the difference between a pending measure and an approved extension is significant.
As for the banks, the source lists the UBS Act among the unfinished projects: the Council of States has approved 90% of the funding. This distinction avoids confusing a chamber’s decision with the closure of the dossier. Regarding the banking chapter, readers can cross-reference this analysis with conti bancari in Svizzera.
Finally, the revision of the TTPCP provides a clear comparison over time: starting in 2031, electric trucks will also be subject to the tax, whereas today 90% of heavy-duty vehicles fall into the least expensive category. For those in the transportation industry, this session provides a future date and a snapshot of the current system.
## Recommended tools For an updated estimate, use the net salary calculator and the CHF-EUR exchange comparator. ## What to Keep an Eye On Now
To track these issues without confusing approvals, proposals, and referendums, monitoring can be organized into five key areas.
### Five Key Areas to Monitor
1. Bilateral Agreements III. Mark the National Council as the next key step. The decision will then require a double majority of the people and the cantons: the vote in the Council of States alone does not conclude the process.
2. Mercosur. Keep the agreement adopted by Parliament separate from the referendum already announced by civil society organizations. The source indicates that the final say should rest with the people.
3. VAT. In the hotel sector, note the extension of the reduced rate of 3.8% through 2031. Regarding military funding, consider the 0.2% rate through 2045 as a proposal from the Council of States awaiting consideration by the other chamber.
4. TTPCP. If you follow heavy-duty transportation, note that 2031 is the year when electric trucks will also be subject to the tax, and compare this with the current figure of 90% of vehicles in the lowest-cost category.
5. Severance Pay. For executives in the Federal Administration and parastatal companies, distinguish between the ban on payments and terminations not attributable to the employee, such as those resulting from reorganization.
The calendar provides an additional point of reference: the winter session will be held from November 30 to December 18. For future crises, the key point to examine will be the detailed justification that the Federal Council must provide for each invocation of the right of necessity—a decision made in light of the experiences of the pandemic and the recent UBS crisis.
Meanwhile, the revision of the Electrical Installations Act, the Electricity Supply Act, the abolition of the statute of limitations for murder, the extension of the simplified hiring process for doctors, the amendment to the supervision of insurers, and the partial revision of the Federal Supreme Court Act are among the items approved.
For fur purchases, practical oversight takes place at the time of purchase: Swiss fur shops, clothing stores, and online retailers will be required to indicate the production method and provide proof that no suffering was inflicted on the animals. Regarding foie gras, the counterproposal focuses instead on labeling and reducing sales.
To see the impact of the VAT and daily costs proposals, consult costo della vita in Svizzera. To relate the decisions to your income, use calcolatore stipendio.

## At a Glance - Chiasso and Mendrisio support professional reintegration - First individual interview scheduled for October - Four sessions between November and December at LaFilanda - Free participation with childcare services
## Key Facts - Organizers → Cities of Chiasso and Mendrisio - Location → LaFilanda in Mendrisio - Dates → November 19 and 24, December 1 and 10 - Follow-up → individual interviews and four sessions in 2027
### The First Session and Follow-Up
In October, the first step is an individual interview. This marks the start of the “Work-Life Balance and Professional Reintegration” series of sessions, offered by the Cities of Chiasso and Mendrisio at LaFilanda in Mendrisio.
The initiative stems from a specific challenge: returning to work after a period devoted entirely to motherhood can seem, to many new mothers, an immense and insurmountable challenge. The program is therefore aimed at mothers and women who want to take stock of their situation and begin the process of re-entering the workforce. To support the search for new opportunities, participants can also follow up on this topic through the annunci di lavoro program.
The program description summarizes the objective as follows: > “A program designed for mothers and women who wish to assess their situation and take the first steps toward re-entering the workforce. Information, guidance, and advice on finding work-life balance solutions, rediscovering their skills, and applying for jobs with greater confidence.”
The areas highlighted in the presentation are finding work-life balance solutions, rediscovering one’s skills, and gaining greater confidence in job applications. The program thus combines guidance, information, and advice aimed at facilitating the transition back to work.
Following the initial interview, four group sessions are scheduled at LaFilanda: on November 19 and 24, then on December 1 and 10. In 2027, individual follow-up interviews are planned, interspersed with four new group training sessions.

The practical logic of the proposal lies in the sequence of different stages. The structure can be understood as follows:
| Element | Specified Detail | |---|---| | Start | individual interview in October | | Objectives | work-life balance, skills, and job applications | | Follow-up | individual interviews and four group meetings in 2027 |

The description places it at the beginning, before the four group meetings; the overall program then focuses on information, guidance, and advice, with an emphasis on work-life balance, skills, and job applications.
The training component is explicitly addressed in the follow-up phase in 2027, when the individual support interviews are supplemented by four new group sessions. For those who need to balance attending the sessions with childcare, these two details should be considered together with the location: the program lists both the sessions and the service at the same venue.
This initiative can be complemented by a consultation regarding congedo parentale, keeping the period dedicated to maternity leave and the phase of professional reintegration distinct. The program offered in Chiasso and Mendrisio remains focused on career guidance, skills development, and job applications.

Anyone who wants to follow the program can turn the available information into a simple schedule. The key is to follow the order in which the initiative was presented.

Making this distinction helps ensure you don’t miss any of the scheduled appointments. - Third: During the meetings, focus on the three objectives outlined in the presentation: finding work-life balance solutions, rediscovering your skills, and applying for jobs with greater confidence. - Fourth: Start thinking about the follow-up planned for 2027. After the first phase, individual support sessions are scheduled, interspersed with four new group training sessions. - Fifth: Include the babysitting service available at LaFilanda in your plans. The work can therefore focus on the first steps, the skills to be rediscovered, and work-life balance solutions to be evaluated along the way.

item.title: Bankruptcies on the rise. And Ticino is above average
item.description: In the first nine months of the year, corporate bankruptcies in Switzerland rose to 11,412 (+37%). Ticino recorded 721 bankruptcies, an increase of 48%.
item.content:encoded:
## At a Glance - 11,412 bankruptcies in the first nine months, up 37% nationwide - Ticino reports 721 bankruptcies: up 48%, above the average - The change effective January 1, 2025, concerns tax debts - 40,487 new companies established during the same period, +2%
## Key Facts - Period → first nine months of the year - Bankruptcies in Switzerland → 11,412 - National change → 37% compared to 2025 - Ticino → 721 bankruptcies, +48% - New companies → 40,487, +2% - Source → Crif
In the first nine months of the year, there were 11,412 corporate bankruptcies in Switzerland, representing a 37% increase compared to the same period in 2025. Ticino ranks above the national average: bankruptcies in the canton reached 721, representing a 48% increase.
The data was published by Crif, a company active in anti-fraud measures, credit checks, and providing information to businesses and individuals. The survey highlights two distinct trends: businesses affected by bankruptcy and those incorporated during the same time period.
### Sectors and Regions
Among the sectors listed, construction saw 1,380 companies affected by bankruptcies, a 13% increase. The restaurant industry reached 1,019, with a 20% increase, while the retail sector recorded 895 cases and a 51% increase.
The regional picture is mixed. In addition to Ticino, Graubünden also exceeds the national average: 218 bankruptcies, up 95%. In absolute terms, Zurich reached 1,850 cases, up 28%; Geneva, 1,369, up 65%; and Vaud, 1,006, up 30%.
One reason for the increase, according to Crif, is the legislative change that took effect on January 1, 2025. As of that date, tax debts owed by companies listed in the commercial register can be enforced through bankruptcy proceedings. Previously, authorities could collect unpaid taxes only through seizure.
During the same period, 40,487 new companies were established, a 2% increase year-over-year. Business consulting saw 3,499 new companies (+25%), real estate 3,032 (+6%), construction 2,896 (+5%), and retail 2,823 (-12%). At the cantonal level, Ticino saw 1,806 new companies (+9%) and Graubünden 853 (+8.1%). ## What Has Changed in the Analysis
A 48% increase in Ticino does not allow us to determine how many bankruptcies were caused by the tax change. Crif presents it as one of the reasons for the increase, but does not break down the portion linked to tax debts in the published data. This distinction prevents us from turning a temporal correlation into a single cause.
### The Before-and-After Comparison
For a company listed in the commercial register, the shift from collecting unpaid taxes solely through seizure to the option of enforcing them through bankruptcy proceedings changes the procedural framework described by the source. The date to consider as the turning point is January 1, 2025. However, tax amounts, payment deadlines, or required documents are not specified: including them would go beyond the available data.
Sector-specific figures should also be considered separately. The construction sector appears both among the 1,380 companies affected by bankruptcies (13%) and among new businesses (2,896, up 5%). Retail, on the other hand, recorded 895 bankruptcies (+51%), while new businesses in the sector totaled 2,823 (-12%). The two sets of data do not necessarily describe the same businesses and cannot be automatically balanced. Business consulting, with 3,499 new businesses and a 25% increase, and the real estate sector, with 3,032 and a 6% increase, show where new business openings are concentrated, not how many businesses will remain operational.
Geographically, Ticino recorded 721 bankruptcies and 1,806 new companies; Graubünden recorded 218 and 853. The respective increases—48% and 9% in Ticino, 95% and 8.1% in Graubünden—reflect two distinct trends. To compare risk across cantons, a ratio based on the total number of businesses would be needed, a figure the source does not provide. The absolute figures for Zurich, Geneva, and Vaud, while high, are not sufficient on their own to measure the probability of bankruptcy.
For those looking for indicators related to the labor market, the survey does not provide figures on employment, layoffs, or hiring. The aziende che assumono page can be consulted, but it should not be presented as an automatic consequence of the CRIF data.
## Recommended tools For an updated estimate, use the net salary calculator and the CHF-EUR exchange comparator. ## Checklist for Businesses and Readers
This source provides a systematic assessment but does not calculate individual risk. To use the data without adding external information, it is best to proceed in distinct steps.
### 1. Identify the Scope
Determine whether you are examining a company listed in the commercial register. For this category, the source describes the possibility, effective January 1, 2025, of enforcing tax debts through bankruptcy proceedings. Do not interpret this wording as a rule applicable to all businesses: the text does not state that.
### 2. Distinguish the tax-specific case from the general information
If the issue is a tax debt, note the comparison indicated by the source: previously, unpaid taxes were collected through seizure, whereas as of 2025, bankruptcy proceedings are also mentioned. The source does not provide amounts, deadlines, competent agencies, or forms. The verification possible here therefore concerns the distinction between the procedure prior to the amendment and the one following it.
### 3. Analyze the sector and the region separately
Compare the company’s industry sector with the separate data sets for bankruptcies and new businesses. Do not add bankruptcies and new business openings together, and do not treat the increase in new businesses as evidence of stability. For geographic data, note the canton and decide whether to compare percentage changes or absolute values; do not mix the two criteria.
### 4. Use the data as a signal, not as a verdict
Anyone evaluating a job or a career change can use the survey as a general indicator and then verify the offers in the annunci di lavoro database. The text does not contain individual data on specific companies, so it does not allow you to determine whether a company is financially sound or in trouble.
To maintain the correct context, do not confuse this statistic with other figures in the material: the 3.7% refers to the increase in health insurance funds in Ticino for 2027, while 312 km/h refers to a news story from France. These figures are unrelated to corporate bankruptcies.
To complete the verification of personal income using a separate tool, use calcolatore stipendio.

item.title: AIL Compensation and Transparency: The MPS Inquiry
item.description: Giuseppe Sergi and Matteo Pronzini question the Council of State regarding AIL compensation and the protection of public assets.
item.content:encoded:
## In Brief - Giuseppe Sergi questioned the State Council - The document was signed by Matteo Pronzini - AIL compensation: 20,000–90,000 francs in the first half of 2026 - AIL is wholly owned by the City of Lugano
## Key Facts - Who → Giuseppe Sergi, with Matteo Pronzini - Company → AIL, a private-law corporation - Ownership → 100% City of Lugano - Activities → distribution of electricity, water, gas, and thermal energy - Period → first half of 2026 - Compensation → approximately 20,000–90,000 francs - Variables → role, commissions, and meetings - Topic → corporate autonomy, transparency, and public assets
Giuseppe Sergi submitted a parliamentary question to the State Council regarding the management of wholly publicly owned companies and transparency. The motion was co-signed by Matteo Pronzini and was prompted by the discussion on the compensation of members of the Board of Directors of Aziende Industriali di Lugano (AIL).
According to data cited in the parliamentary motion, in the first half of 2026, the compensation for members of the AIL Board of Directors ranged, depending on their role and participation in committees and meetings, from approximately 20,000 to 90,000 francs. For the MPS, this range raises a broader question: how to balance the company’s autonomy with the protection of public assets.
AIL is a private-law corporation, but it is wholly owned by the City of Lugano. It operates in the distribution of electricity, water, gas, and heat. It is precisely this combination—a private legal form and wholly public ownership—that raises questions regarding the oversight and obligations of the City as the owner.
### From the Figures to the Institutional Issue

item.title: Starting a Business in Graubünden: A Guide to Costs and Taxes
item.description: From Legal Structure to Payroll Taxes: A Practical Guide to the Three Tax Levels and Social Security Obligations for Those Starting a Business in Graubünden.
item.content:encoded:
## At a Glance - Three levels of taxation: federal, cantonal, and municipal - AFC/ESTV administers federal income tax (IFD) and VAT - Legal form, registration, capital, and taxes are separate categories - Payroll contributions are separate from taxes
## Key Facts - Taxes → Federal, cantonal, and municipal income tax - AVS/AI/IPG → 5.3% employee contribution; 10.6% total - AD/AC → 1.1% up to the annual cap - LAINF/LAA → 0.7–1.5% depending on the sector - LPP/BVG → 7%, 10%, 15%, 18% by age group
Direct federal tax, cantonal tax, and municipal tax constitute the three distinct tax levels that must be kept separate, even when planning to start a business in the Canton of Graubünden. Each canton has its own law and its own multiplier; for municipalities, the multiplier is applied to the cantonal rate. Therefore, the table cannot be interpreted as showing a single tax rate applicable throughout Switzerland.
### The Initial Dossier
Research on how to start a business in the Canton of Graubünden—covering the commercial register and associated costs—begins with four key elements: choice of legal structure, registration with the commercial register, minimum capital, and registration fees. These are the categories that must be addressed side by side in the business launch plan. The minimum capital and registration fees should not be treated as a single item, just as registration does not replace the choice of legal form. The budget must keep these considerations separate.
Institutional jurisdiction must also be assigned correctly. The AFC/ESTV is the authority for direct federal tax and VAT. Cantonal administrations, on the other hand, handle cantonal and municipal taxation. The Federal Social Insurance Office (UFAS/BSV) oversees social security, including AVS/AI and LPP, but does not set taxes; the Federal Statistical Office (UST/BFS) produces statistics and does not establish tax rates.
This overview is useful even before registration. Those preparing the application can separate tax-related questions from social security-related ones, avoiding the need to seek a tax rate or percentage from the wrong agency. For the personal portion of the calculation, the calcolatore stipendio e imposte helps interpret the tax burden without replacing cantonal verifications. ### When Salaries Come Into Play
The transition from a business that does not pay salaries to one with employees changes how costs are reported. Direct federal income tax and VAT remain within the tax scope, but payroll taxes require a separate line item. The percentages to be included in the budget allow you to set up the calculation without mixing up bonuses, taxes, and social security contributions.
| Item | Data to Consider | | AVS/AI/IPG | 5.3% for the employee; 10.6% total including the employer | | AD/AC | 1.1% up to the annual cap | | LAINF/LAA | 0.7–1.5% depending on the sector | | LPP/BVG | Coordinated salary: 7% (25–34), 10% (35–44), 15% (45–54), 18% (55+ up to the reference age) |
The first three items do not have the same basis indicated: AVS/AI/IPG distinguishes the employee’s share from the total with the employer, AD/AC is linked to the annual cap, and LAINF/LAA varies by sector. LPP/BVG, on the other hand, is based on the coordinated salary, and the indicated percentage increases in the age groups 25–34, 35–44, 45–54, and 55 and older, up to the reference age. A budget for the Canton of Graubünden must therefore avoid applying a single percentage rate to every salary.
### Personal Costs Not to Be Confused
The LAMal/KVG follows a different logic. It is mandatory for residents, must be taken out within 3 months of arrival, involves per-capita premiums, and is neither a tax nor a payroll contribution. Premiums vary by canton and region; premium reductions are a cantonal subsidy. For those starting a business and living in Switzerland, this item relates to personal living expenses, not the payroll contribution schedule.
Employment regulations also have national thresholds that must be factored into planning. There is no federal minimum wage, though some cantons have their own. The maximum workweek is 45 hours in manufacturing, office work, and retail, or 50 hours in other sectors. The minimum vacation time is 4 weeks, which increases to 5 weeks for those under 20 years of age. Cantonal regulations cannot be replaced by a single national rule.
To interpret these items in practice, you can refer to the guide on busta paga svizzera alongside the guide on AVS/LPP e rendita.
## Useful planning tools To estimate your pension strategy, use the pension planner and the pillar 3 simulator. ### Operational Checklist
- Determine the legal form and itemize the minimum capital, commercial registry registration, and registration fees in the plan. - Assign audits to the appropriate authority: AFC/ESTV for direct federal tax and VAT; cantonal administrations for cantonal and municipal taxes. - If the business employs staff, distinguish between AVS/AI/IPG, AD/AC, LAINF/LAA, and LPP/BVG, applying the relevant percentages and age brackets. - Check the employment framework: absence of a federal minimum wage, any applicable cantonal regulations, maximum workweek of 45 or 50 hours, and minimum vacation time of 4 or 5 weeks. - Separate the personal coverage: for residents, KVG enrollment within 3 months of arrival; for figures and thresholds, use the annual data from the official source.
The first page of the dossier can clearly distinguish the legal structure, the commercial register, the minimum capital requirement, and registration fees. This format avoids adding a social security percentage to a tax rate or treating a LAMal premium as an employer contribution. In the section on personnel, the items should then be compared with the sector, age group, and coordinated salary specified for LPP/BVG.
### Updating the Figures
Figures that are indexed annually should not be frozen in a spreadsheet; these include the unemployment insurance (AD/AC) ceiling, the BVG coordination threshold and deduction, average LAMal premiums, and the median wage. The cost plan must therefore specify the reference year and refer to the official source when the amount is needed. This same approach prevents pension or insurance data from being treated as a tax rate.
For the reporting section, you can open the dichiarazione delle imposte form and verify the federal, cantonal, and municipal levels separately. Before finalizing your personal budget, use the calcolatore stipendio e imposte form.
